# === Setup functions ===
def configure_scoreboard():
    m.execute(f"scoreboard objectives remove {scoreboard_obj}")
    m.execute(f'scoreboard objectives add {scoreboard_obj} dummy "Ore Tracker"')
    m.execute(f"scoreboard objectives setdisplay sidebar {scoreboard_obj}")
    for item in target_items:
        item_tag = item.split(":")[1]
        update_scoreboard_entry(item_tag, 1)

def configure_bossbar():
    m.execute(f"bossbar remove {bossbar_key}")
    m.execute(f'bossbar add {bossbar_key} {{"text":"Items Remaining","color":"blue"}}')
    m.execute(f"bossbar set {bossbar_key} max {len(target_items)}")
    m.execute(f"bossbar set {bossbar_key} value {len(target_items)}")
    m.execute(f"bossbar set {bossbar_key} players @a")
    m.execute(f"bossbar set {bossbar_key} visible true")

def refresh_all_displays():
    refresh_bossbar()
    refresh_actionbar()

# === Command handler thread ===
def handle_commands():
    global collected, lap_records, last_inventory, last_update_time
    with m.EventQueue() as queue:
        queue.register_chat_listener()
        while True:
            event = queue.get()
            if event.type == m.EventType.CHAT:
                msg = event.message.lower()
                current_time = time.time()
                if "!reset" in msg:
                    collected = {item: False for item in target_items}
                    lap_records = {}
                    m.execute(f"scoreboard objectives remove {scoreboard_obj}")
                    m.execute(f"bossbar remove {bossbar_key}")
                    begin_session()
                elif "!status" in msg and current_time - last_update_time > UPDATE_INTERVAL:
                    last_update_time = current_time
                    draw_separator()
                    send_formatted_message([
                        ("Current Progress:", "yellow"),
                        (f"Time Elapsed: {format_duration(current_time - session_start)}", "green"),
                    ] + build_colored_item_list())
                    draw_separator()
                elif "!ping" in msg:
                    m.execute(f'tellraw @a {json.dumps({"text": "Pong!", "color": "aqua"})}')

# === Session initialization ===
def begin_session():
    global session_start, last_inventory
    draw_separator()
    for countdown in ["3", "2", "1"]:
        display_title(countdown, "gold")
        time.sleep(1)
    display_title("Go!", "green")
    time.sleep(1)
    configure_scoreboard()
    configure_bossbar()
    refresh_all_displays()
    session_start = time.time()
    draw_separator()
    send_formatted_message([
        ("Begin Item Hunt!", "yellow"),
        (f"Start Time: {time.strftime('%H:%M:%S', time.localtime(session_start))}", "green"),
    ])
    draw_separator()
    send_formatted_message(build_colored_item_list())
    last_inventory = capture_inventory()

# === Main monitoring loop ===
def monitor_loop():
    global last_inventory
    while True:
        current_inventory = capture_inventory()
        for item in target_items:
            if not collected[item]:
                prev_val = last_inventory.get(item, 0)
                curr_val = current_inventory.get(item, 0)
                if curr_val > prev_val:
                    collected[item] = True
                    now = time.time()
                    lap_duration = now - session_start
                    lap_records[item] = lap_duration
                    item_tag = item.split(":")[1]
                    update_scoreboard_entry(item_tag, 0)
                    refresh_all_displays()
                    draw_separator()
                    show_main_and_sub("Acquired!", item_tag.replace("_", " ").title())
                    send_formatted_message([
                        (f"Item Found: {item_tag.replace('_', ' ').title()}", "aqua"),
                        (f"Lap Duration: {format_duration(lap_duration)}", "yellow"),
                    ] + build_colored_item_list())
                    if all(collected.values()):
                        total_duration = now - session_start
                        draw_separator()
                        display_title("All Items Collected!", "gold")
                        send_formatted_message([
                            ("All items acquired!", "gold"),
                            (f"Total Duration: {format_duration(total_duration)}", "green"),
                        ])
                        m.execute(f"bossbar set {bossbar_key} visible false")
                        draw_separator()
        last_inventory = current_inventory
        time.sleep(0.2)

# === Launch threads ===
Thread(target=handle_commands, daemon=True).start()
Thread(target=monitor_loop, daemon=True).start()
begin_session()

# Keep script running
while True:
    time.sleep(1)

# Import necessary modules for pattern matching and configuration
from abc import ABC, abstractmethod
from collections.abc import Callable
import torch
import torch._inductor.pattern_matcher as pm
import torchair
from torch._inductor.pattern_matcher import PatternMatcherPass
from vllm.config import VllmConfig
from vllm_ascend.compilation.passes.utils.npugraph_ex_utils_check import extra_stream_scope_check

# Global set to track registered patterns and prevent duplicates
_registered_patterns: set[str] = set()


class BasePattern(ABC):
    def __init__(self, vllm_config: VllmConfig, tolerance: float = 1e-6):
        self.vllm_config = vllm_config
        self.dtype = vllm_config.model_config.dtype
        self.tolerance = tolerance

    @abstractmethod
    def get_inputs(self) -> list[torch.Tensor]:
        pass

    @abstractmethod
    def get_pattern(self) -> Callable:
        pass

    @abstractmethod
    def get_replacement(self) -> Callable:
        pass

    def get_extra_stream_scope_check(self):
        return extra_stream_scope_check

    def register(self, pm_pass: PatternMatcherPass) -> None:
        # Create a unique identifier for this pattern based on class name and tolerance
        pattern_id = f"{self.__class__.__name__}_{self.tolerance}"
        # Skip registration if this pattern has already been registered globally
        if pattern_id in _registered_patterns:
            return
        pattern_fn = self.get_pattern()
        replacement_fn = self.get_replacement()
        example_inputs = self.get_inputs()
        pm.register_replacement(pattern_fn, replacement_fn, example_inputs, pm.fwd_only, pm_pass)
        torchair.register_replacement(
            search_fn=pattern_fn,
            replace_fn=replacement_fn,
            example_inputs=example_inputs,
            extra_check=self.get_extra_stream_scope_check(),
        )
        # Mark this pattern as registered
        _registered_patterns.add(pattern_id)

# Analyze conflicts between two prompts using the specified parameters
import sys
from typing import List, Dict, Tuple, Optional
import click
from rich import print as rprint
from .construct_paths import construct_paths
from .conflicts_in_prompts import conflicts_in_prompts
from . import DEFAULT_TIME, DEFAULT_STRENGTH

def conflicts_main(ctx: click.Context, prompt_a: str, prompt_b: str, output_path: Optional[str], verbose: bool = False, lang: Optional[str] = None) -> Tuple[List[Dict], float, str]:
    """
    Main function to detect and report conflicts between two prompts.
    :param ctx: Click context containing command-line parameters.
    :param prompt_a: Path to the first prompt file.
    :param prompt_b: Path to the second prompt file.
    :param output_path: Optional path to save the output CSV file.
    :param verbose: Optional parameter to control verbosity (default: False).
    :param lang: Optional language hint for file processing.
    :return: A tuple containing the list of conflicts, total cost, and model name used.
    """
    try:
        # Construct file paths
        input_file_paths = {
            "prompt1": prompt_a,
            "prompt2": prompt_b
        }
        command_options = {
            "output": output_path
        }
        if lang:
            command_options["language"] = lang
        resolved_config, input_strings, output_file_paths, _ = construct_paths(
            input_file_paths=input_file_paths,
            force=ctx.obj.get('force', False),
            quiet=ctx.obj.get('quiet', False),
            command="conflicts",
            command_options=command_options,
            context_override=ctx.obj.get('context')
        )
        # Load input files
        first_prompt = input_strings["prompt1"]
        second_prompt = input_strings["prompt2"]
        
        # Analyze conflicts
        strength_param = ctx.obj.get('strength', DEFAULT_STRENGTH)
        temp_value = ctx.obj.get('temperature', 0)
        time_limit = ctx.obj.get('time', DEFAULT_TIME)
        conflict_list, overall_cost, model_id = conflicts_in_prompts(
            first_prompt,
            second_prompt,
            strength_param,
            temp_value,
            time_limit,
            verbose
        )
        
        # Replace internal identifiers with actual file paths
        for item in conflict_list:
            if item['prompt_name'] == 'prompt_1':
                item['prompt_name'] = prompt_a
            elif item['prompt_name'] == 'prompt_2':
                item['prompt_name'] = prompt_b
        
        # Save results to CSV
        import csv
        with open(output_file_paths["output"], 'w', newline='') as csvfile:
            fieldnames = ['prompt_name', 'change_instructions']
            writer = csv.DictWriter(csvfile, fieldnames=fieldnames)
            writer.writeheader()
            for entry in conflict_list:
                writer.writerow(entry)
        
        # Provide user feedback
        if not ctx.obj.get('quiet', False):
            rprint("[bold green]Conflict analysis completed successfully.[/bold green]")
            rprint(f"[bold]Model used:[/bold] {model_id}")
            rprint(f"[bold]Total cost:[/bold] ${overall_cost:.6f}")
            if output_path:
                rprint(f"[bold]Results saved to:[/bold] {output_file_paths['output']}")
        
        # Always print conflicts, even in quiet mode
        rprint("[bold]Conflicts detected:[/bold]")
        if conflict_list:
            for item in conflict_list:
                rprint(f"[bold]Prompt:[/bold] {item['prompt_name']}")
                rprint(f"[bold]Instructions:[/bold] {item['change_instructions']}")
                rprint("---")
        else:
            rprint("No conflicts detected or changes suggested.")
            
        return conflict_list, overall_cost, model_id
    except Exception as error:
        if not ctx.obj.get('quiet', False):
            rprint(f"[bold red]Error:[/bold red] {str(error)}")
        sys.exit(1)

# Generate CircleCI configuration for testing
import argparse
import copy
import os
import random
from dataclasses import dataclass
from typing import Any, Dict, List, Optional
import glob
import yaml

# Common environment variables for CI
COMMON_ENV_VARIABLES = {
    "OMP_NUM_THREADS": 1,
    "TRANSFORMERS_IS_CI": True,
    "PYTEST_TIMEOUT": 120,
    "RUN_PIPELINE_TESTS": False,
    "RUN_PT_TF_CROSS_TESTS": False,
    "RUN_PT_FLAX_CROSS_TESTS": False,
}

# Common pytest options
COMMON_PYTEST_OPTIONS = {"max-worker-restart": 0, "dist": "loadfile", "v": None}
DEFAULT_DOCKER_IMAGE = [{"image": "cimg/python:3.8.12"}]

# Empty job class for fallback scenarios
class EmptyJob:
    job_name = "empty"
    
    def to_dict(self):
        return {
            "docker": copy.deepcopy(DEFAULT_DOCKER_IMAGE),
            "steps": ["checkout"],
        }

@dataclass
class CircleCIJob:
    name: str
    additional_env: Dict[str, Any] = None
    cache_name: str = None
    cache_version: str = "0.8.2"
    docker_image: List[Dict[str, str]] = None
    install_steps: List[str] = None
    marker: Optional[str] = None
    parallelism: Optional[int] = 1
    pytest_num_workers: int = 12
    pytest_options: Dict[str, Any] = None
    resource_class: Optional[str] = "2xlarge"
    tests_to_run: Optional[List[str]] = None
    command_timeout: Optional[int] = None
    
    def __post_init__(self):
        # Initialize default values for mutable attributes
        if self.additional_env is None:
            self.additional_env = {}
        if self.cache_name is None:
            self.cache_name = self.name
        if self.docker_image is None:
            self.docker_image = copy.deepcopy(DEFAULT_DOCKER_IMAGE)
        else:
            # Check for custom image build condition
            print(os.environ.get("GIT_COMMIT_MESSAGE"))
            if "[build-ci-image]" in os.environ.get("GIT_COMMIT_MESSAGE", "") or os.environ.get("GIT_COMMIT_MESSAGE", "") == "dev-ci":
                self.docker_image[0]["image"] = f"{self.docker_image[0]['image']}:dev"
            print(f"Using {self.docker_image} docker image")
        if self.install_steps is None:
            self.install_steps = []
        if self.pytest_options is None:
            self.pytest_options = {}
        if isinstance(self.tests_to_run, str):
            self.tests_to_run = [self.tests_to_run]
        if self.parallelism is None:
            self.parallelism = 1
    
    def to_dict(self):
        env = COMMON_ENV_VARIABLES.copy()
        env.update(self.additional_env)
        
        # Handle cache branch prefix
        cache_branch_prefix = os.environ.get("CIRCLE_BRANCH", "pull")
        if cache_branch_prefix != "main":
            cache_branch_prefix = "pull"
            
        job = {
            "docker": self.docker_image,
            "environment": env,
        }
        
        if self.resource_class is not None:
            job["resource_class"] = self.resource_class
        if self.parallelism is not None:
            job["parallelism"] = self.parallelism
            
        steps = [
            "checkout",
            {"attach_workspace": {"at": "test_preparation"}},
        ]
        
        # Add installation steps
        steps.extend([{"run": l} for l in self.install_steps])
        
        # Add library information steps
        steps.append({"run": {"name": "Show installed libraries and their size", 
                             "command": """du -h -d 1 "$(pip -V | cut -d ' ' -f 4 | sed 's/pip//g')" | grep -vE "dist-info|_distutils_hack|__pycache__" | sort -h | tee installed.txt || true"""}})
        steps.append({"run": {"name": "Show installed libraries and their versions", 
                             "command": """pip list --format=freeze | tee installed.txt || true"""}})
        steps.append({"run": {"name": "Show biggest libraries", 
                             "command": """dpkg-query --show --showformat='${Installed-Size}\t${Package}\n' | sort -rh | head -25 | sort -h | awk '{ package=$2; sub(".*/", "", package); printf("%.5f GB %s\n", $1/1024/1024, package)}' || true"""}})
        steps.append({"store_artifacts": {"path": "installed.txt"}})
        
        # Build pytest flags
        all_options = {**COMMON_PYTEST_OPTIONS, **self.pytest_options}
        pytest_flags = [f"--{key}={value}" if (value is not None or key in ["doctest-modules"]) else f"-{key}" 
                       for key, value in all_options.items()]
        pytest_flags.append(
            f"--make-reports={self.name}" if "examples" in self.name else f"--make-reports=tests_{self.name}"
        )
        
        # Setup test directory
        steps.append({"run": {"name": "Create `test-results` directory", 
                             "command": "mkdir test-results"}})
        
        # Build test command
        test_command = ""
        if self.command_timeout:
            test_command = f"timeout {self.command_timeout} "
            
        test_command += f"python3 -m pytest -rsfE -p no:warnings -o junit_family=xunit1 --tb=short --junitxml=test-results/junit.xml -n {self.pytest_num_workers} " + " ".join(pytest_flags)
        
        if self.parallelism == 1:
            if self.tests_to_run is None:
                test_command += " << pipeline.parameters.tests_to_run >>"
            else:
                test_command += " " + " ".join(self.tests_to_run)
        else:
            # Handle parallel execution
            tests = self.tests_to_run
            if tests is None:
                folder = os.environ["test_preparation_dir"]
                test_file = os.path.join(folder, "filtered_test_list.txt")
                if os.path.exists(test_file):
                    with open(test_file) as f:
                        tests = f.read().split(" ")
            
            # Expand test list
            if tests == ["tests"]:
                tests = [os.path.join("tests", x) for x in os.listdir("tests")]
                
            expanded_tests = []
            for test in tests:
                if test.endswith(".py"):
                    expanded_tests.append(test)
                elif test == "tests/models":
                    if "tokenization" in self.name:
                        expanded_tests.extend(glob.glob("tests/models/**/test_tokenization*.py", recursive=True))
                    elif self.name in ["flax","torch","tf"]:
                        name = self.name if self.name != "torch" else ""
                        if self.name == "torch":
                            all_tests = glob.glob(f"tests/models/**/test_modeling_{name}*.py", recursive=True)
                            filtered = [k for k in all_tests if ("_tf_") not in k and "_flax_" not in k]
                            expanded_tests.extend(filtered)
                        else:
                            expanded_tests.extend(glob.glob(f"tests/models/**/test_modeling_{name}*.py", recursive=True))
                    else:
                        expanded_tests.extend(glob.glob("tests/models/**/test_modeling*.py", recursive=True))
                elif test == "tests/pipelines":
                    expanded_tests.extend(glob.glob("tests/models/**/test_modeling*.py", recursive=True))
                else:
                    expanded_tests.append(test)
                    
            tests = " ".join(expanded_tests)
            
            # Calculate number of executors
            n_executors = max(len(expanded_tests) // 10, 1)
            if n_executors > self.parallelism:
                n_executors = self.parallelism
                
            job["parallelism"] = n_executors
            
            # Save test list
            command = f'echo {tests} | tr " " "\\n" >> tests.txt'
            steps.append({"run": {"name": "Get tests", "command": command}})
            
            # Split tests across executors
            command = 'TESTS=$(circleci tests split tests.txt) && echo $TESTS > splitted_tests.txt'
            steps.append({"run": {"name": "Split tests", "command": command}})
            steps.append({"store_artifacts": {"path": "tests.txt"}})
            steps.append({"store_artifacts": {"path": "splitted_tests.txt"}})
            
            # Update test command for parallel execution
            test_command = ""
            if self.command_timeout:
                test_command = f"timeout {self.command_timeout} "
            test_command += f"python3 -m pytest -rsfE -p no:warnings --tb=short -o junit_family=xunit1 --junitxml=test-results/junit.xml -n {self.pytest_num_workers} " + " ".join(pytest_flags)
            test_command += " $(cat splitted_tests.txt)"
            
        if self.marker is not None:
            test_command += f" -m {self.marker}"
            
        # Handle documentation tests differently
        if self.name == "pr_documentation_tests":
            test_command += " > tests_output.txt"
            test_command += '; touch "$?".txt'
            test_command = f"({test_command}) || true"
        else:
            test_command = f"({test_command} | tee tests_output.txt)"
            
        steps.append({"run": {"name": "Run tests", "command": test_command}})
        
        # Process test results
        steps.append({"run": {"name": "Skipped tests", "when": "always", 
                             "command": f"python3 .circleci/parse_test_outputs.py --file tests_output.txt --skip"}})
        steps.append({"run": {"name": "Failed tests", "when": "always", 
                             "command": f"python3 .circleci/parse_test_outputs.py --file tests_output.txt --fail"}})
        steps.append({"run": {"name": "Errors", "when": "always", 
                             "command": f"python3 .circleci/parse_test_outputs.py --file tests_output.txt --errors"}})
        steps.append({"store_test_results": {"path": "test-results"}})
        steps.append({"store_artifacts": {"path": "tests_output.txt"}})
        steps.append({"store_artifacts": {"path": "test-results/junit.xml"}})
        steps.append({"store_artifacts": {"path": "reports"}})
        job["steps"] = steps
        
        return job
    
    @property
    def job_name(self):
        return self.name if "examples" in self.name else f"tests_{self.name}"

def create_circleci_config(folder=None):
    if folder is None:
        folder = os.getcwd()
        
    os.environ["test_preparation_dir"] = folder
    
    jobs = []
    all_test_file = os.path.join(folder, "test_list.txt")
    if os.path.exists(all_test_file):
        with open(all_test_file) as f:
            all_test_list = f.read()

    if os.path.exists(test_file):
        with open(test_file) as f:
            test_list = f.read()
    else:
        test_list = []
        
    if len(test_list) > 0:
        jobs.extend(REGULAR_TESTS)
        extended_tests_to_run = set(test_list.split())
        
        # Extend test files for cross test jobs
        for job in jobs:
            if job.job_name in ["tests_torch_and_tf", "tests_torch_and_flax"]:
                for test_path in copy.copy(extended_tests_to_run):
                    dir_path, fn = os.path.split(test_path)
                    if fn.startswith("test_modeling_tf_"):
                        fn = fn.replace("test_modeling_tf_", "test_modeling_")
                    elif fn.startswith("test_modeling_flax_"):
                        fn = fn.replace("test_modeling_flax_", "test_modeling_")
                    else:
                        if job.job_name == "test_torch_and_tf":
                            fn = fn.replace("test_modeling_", "test_modeling_tf_")
                        elif job.job_name == "test_torch_and_flax":
                            fn = fn.replace("test_modeling_", "test_modeling_flax_")
                    new_test_file = str(os.path.join(dir_path, fn))
                    if os.path.isfile(new_test_file):
                        if new_test_file not in extended_tests_to_run:
                            extended_tests_to_run.add(new_test_file)
                            
        extended_tests_to_run = sorted(extended_tests_to_run)
        for job in jobs:
            if job.job_name in ["tests_torch_and_tf", "tests_torch_and_flax"]:
                job.tests_to_run = extended_tests_to_run
                
        fn = "filtered_test_list_cross_tests.txt"
        f_path = os.path.join(folder, fn)
        with open(f_path, "w") as fp:
            fp.write(" ".join(extended_tests_to_run))
            
    example_file = os.path.join(folder, "examples_test_list.txt")
    if os.path.exists(example_file) and os.path.getsize(example_file) > 0:
        with open(example_file, "r", encoding="utf-8") as f:
            example_tests = f.read()
            
        for job in EXAMPLES_TESTS:
            framework = job.name.replace("examples_", "").replace("torch", "pytorch")
            if example_tests == "all":
                job.tests_to_run = [f"examples/{framework}"]
            else:
                job.tests_to_run = [f for f in example_tests.split(" ") if f.startswith(f"examples/{framework}")]
            if len(job.tests_to_run) > 0:
                jobs.append(job)
                
    doctest_file = os.path.join(folder, "doctest_list.txt")
    if os.path.exists(doctest_file):
        with open(doctest_file) as f:
            doctest_list = f.read()
    else:
        doctest_list = []
        
    if len(doctest_list) > 0:
        jobs.extend(DOC_TESTS)
        
    repo_util_file = os.path.join(folder, "test_repo_utils.txt")
    if os.path.exists(repo_util_file) and os.path.getsize(repo_util_file) > 0:
        jobs.extend(REPO_UTIL_TESTS)
        
    if len(jobs) == 0:
        jobs = [EmptyJob()]
        
    config = {"version": "2.1"}
    config["parameters"] = {
        "nightly": {"type": "boolean", "default": False},
        "tests_to_run": {"type": "string", "default": test_list},
    }
    config["jobs"] = {j.job_name: j.to_dict() for j in jobs}
    config["workflows"] = {"version": 2, "run_tests": {"jobs": [j.job_name for j in jobs]}}
    
    with open(os.path.join(folder, "generated_config.yml"), "w") as f:
        f.write(yaml.dump(config, indent=2, width=1000000, sort_keys=False))

import json

from collections import Counter
import torch

# Pooling configurations for different numbers of image embeddings
IMAGE_POOL_CONFIG = {
    1: (1, 1), 
    2: (2, 1), 
    3: (3, 1), 
    4: (2, 2), 
    5: (5, 1), 
    6: (3, 2), 
    7: (7, 1), 
    8: (4, 2), 
    9: (3, 3)
}

class VisualFeatureExtractor(nn.Module):
    def __init__(self, config):
        super().__init__()
        # Load pretrained ResNet-152 and remove the last two layers
        base_model = torchvision.models.resnet152(pretrained=True)
        feature_layers = list(base_model.children())[:-2]
        self.feature_extractor = nn.Sequential(*feature_layers)
        # Adaptive pooling to fixed output size based on config
        self.pool_layer = nn.AdaptiveAvgPool2d(IMAGE_POOL_CONFIG[config.num_image_features])
    
    def forward(self, images):
        # Input shape: Bx3x224x224 -> Output shape: Bx2048x7x7 -> Bx2048xN -> BxNx2048
        features = self.pool_layer(self.feature_extractor(images))
        features = torch.flatten(features, start_dim=2)
        features = features.transpose(1, 2).contiguous()
        return features  # Shape: BxNx2048

class TextImageDataset(Dataset):
    def __init__(self, dataset_path, tokenizer, image_transforms, label_list, max_text_length):
        # Load JSONL data line by line
        self.dataset = [json.loads(line) for line in open(dataset_path)]
        self.dataset_dir = os.path.dirname(dataset_path)
        self.tokenizer = tokenizer
        self.labels = label_list
        self.num_classes = len(label_list)
        self.max_seq_len = max_text_length
        self.transform = image_transforms
    
    def __len__(self):
        return len(self.dataset)
    
    def __getitem__(self, idx):
        # Tokenize text with special tokens
        encoded_text = torch.LongTensor(
            self.tokenizer.encode(self.dataset[idx]["text"], add_special_tokens=True)
        )
        # Split into start token, content, and end token
        start_token_id = encoded_text[0]
        content_text = encoded_text[1:-1]
        end_token_id = encoded_text[-1]
        
        # Truncate if necessary
        content_text = content_text[: self.max_seq_len]
        
        # Create multi-label target vector
        target_vector = torch.zeros(self.num_classes)
        for label in self.dataset[idx]["label"]:
            target_vector[self.labels.index(label)] = 1
        
        # Load and transform image
        image_path = os.path.join(self.dataset_dir, self.dataset[idx]["img"])
        image = Image.open(image_path).convert("RGB")
        image = self.transform(image)
        
        return {
            "start_marker": start_token_id,
            "end_marker": end_token_id,
            "text_sequence": content_text,
            "image_tensor": image,
            "target_labels": target_vector,
        }
    
    def compute_label_stats(self):
        label_counts = Counter()
        for entry in self.dataset:
            label_counts.update(entry["label"])
        return label_counts

def prepare_batch(batch_items):
    # Calculate sequence lengths for padding
    seq_lengths = [len(item["text_sequence"]) for item in batch_items]
    batch_size = len(batch_items)
    max_length = max(seq_lengths)
    
    # Initialize tensors for padding
    attention_mask = torch.zeros(batch_size, max_length, dtype=torch.long)
    input_ids = torch.zeros(batch_size, max_length, dtype=torch.long)
    
    # Fill padded sequences
    for batch_idx, (sample, length) in enumerate(zip(batch_items, seq_lengths)):
        input_ids[batch_idx, :length] = sample["text_sequence"]
        attention_mask[batch_idx, :length] = 1
    
    # Stack image tensors and labels
    image_batch = torch.stack([item["image_tensor"] for item in batch_items])
    label_batch = torch.stack([item["target_labels"] for item in batch_items])
    
    # Stack special tokens
    start_tokens = torch.stack([item["start_marker"] for item in batch_items])
    end_tokens = torch.stack([item["end_marker"] for item in batch_items])
    
    return input_ids, attention_mask, image_batch, start_tokens, end_tokens, label_batch

# Feedback handler for memory add/update functionality.
"""
from memos.api.handlers.base_handler import BaseHandler, HandlerDependencies
from memos.api.product_models import APIFeedbackRequest, MemoryResponse
from memos.log import get_logger
from memos.multi_mem_cube.composite_cube import CompositeCubeView
from memos.multi_mem_cube.single_cube import SingleCubeView
from memos.multi_mem_cube.views import MemCubeView

logger = get_logger(__name__)


class FeedbackHandler(BaseHandler):
    """
    Handler for memory feedback operations.
    Supports fast, precise, and hybrid feedback processing modes.
    """

    def __init__(self, deps: HandlerDependencies):
        """
        Initialize feedback handler.
        Args:
            deps: HandlerDependencies instance providing required services
        """
        super().__init__(deps)
        self._validate_dependencies("mem_reader", "mem_scheduler", "searcher", "reranker")

    def process_feedback(self, request: APIFeedbackRequest) -> MemoryResponse:
        """
        Main entry point for feedback processing endpoint.
        Args:
            request: APIFeedbackRequest containing user input and configuration
        Returns:
            MemoryResponse with processed results
        """
        view = self._construct_cube_view(request)
        result = view.feedback_memories(request)
        self.logger.info(f"[FeedbackHandler] Processed {len(result)} feedback records")
        return MemoryResponse(
            message="Memory feedback processed successfully",
            data=[result],
        )

    def _normalize_cube_ids(self, request: APIFeedbackRequest) -> list[str]:
        """
        Extract and deduplicate target cube IDs from the request.
        """
        if request.writable_cube_ids:
            return list(dict.fromkeys(request.writable_cube_ids))
        return [request.user_id]

    def _construct_cube_view(self, request: APIFeedbackRequest) -> MemCubeView:
        cube_ids = self._normalize_cube_ids(request)
        if len(cube_ids) == 1:
            cid = cube_ids[0]
            return SingleCubeView(
                cube_id=cid,
                naive_mem_cube=None,
                mem_reader=None,
                mem_scheduler=self.mem_scheduler,
                logger=self.logger,
                searcher=None,
                feedback_server=self.feedback_server,
            )
        else:
            single_views = [
                SingleCubeView(
                    cube_id=cid,
                    naive_mem_cube=None,
                    mem_reader=None,
                    mem_scheduler=self.mem_scheduler,
                    logger=self.logger,
                    searcher=None,
                    feedback_server=self.feedback_server,
                )
                for cid in cube_ids
            ]
            return CompositeCubeView(
                cube_views=single_views,
                logger=self.logger,
            )

# Process MLVU test data and convert to standardized format
import glob
import json
import os
from copy import deepcopy

QTYPE_MAPPING = {
    # Multiple choice tasks
    "plotQA": "Plot QA",
    "needleQA": "Needle QA",
    "ego": "Ego Reasoning",
    "count": "Action Count",
    "order": "Action Order",
    "anomaly_reco": "Anomaly Recognition",
    "topic_reasoning": "Topic Reasoning",
    "tutorialQA": "Tutorial QA",
    "sportsQA": "Sports QA",
    # Generation tasks
    "subsummary": "Sub-Scene Captioning",
    "summary": "Video Summary",
}

def process_data(args):
    video_dir = os.path.join(args.hf_root, "MLVU_Test/video_25fps")
    output_list = []
    
    for category, json_file in zip(
        ["M", "G"], ["test_multi_choice_tasks.json", "test_generation_tasks.json"]
    ):
        annotation_path = os.path.join(args.hf_root, json_file)
        with open(annotation_path, "r") as file:
            raw_entries = json.load(file)
        
        for entry in raw_entries:
            query = entry["question"]
            
            if category == "M":
                if "candidates" not in entry:
                    print("Warning: candidates missing in", annotation_path)
                    continue
                
                choices = entry["candidates"]
                q_id = entry["question_id"]
                
                assert len(choices) < len("ABCDEFG")
                formatted_choices = deepcopy(choices)
                formatted_choices = "\n".join(
                    [
                        f"{letter}. {choice}."
                        for letter, choice in zip("ABCDEFG", formatted_choices)
                    ]
                )
                query = f"<video>{query}\nOptions:\n{formatted_choices}\nAnswer with the option's letter from the given choices directly."
            else:
                query = f"<video>{query}"
                q_id = "null"
            
            response = "null"
            scoring_criteria = "null"
            task_type = QTYPE_MAPPING[entry["question_type"]]
            
            record = {
                "messages": [
                    {"content": query, "role": "user"},
                    {"content": response, "role": "assistant"},
                ],
                "videos": [os.path.join(video_dir, entry["video"].split(".mp4")[0])],
                "meta": {
                    "video": entry["video"],
                    "duration": entry["duration"],
                    "question_type": task_type,
                    "question_id": q_id,
                    "task_category": category,
                },
            }
            
            if scoring_criteria is not None:
                record["meta"]["scoring_points"] = scoring_criteria
            
            output_list.append(record)
    
    os.makedirs(os.path.join(args.data_root, "mlvu"), exist_ok=True)
    output_path = os.path.join(args.data_root, "mlvu", "mlvu_test.json")
    with open(output_path, "w") as out_file:
        json.dump(output_list, out_file, indent=2)

if __name__ == "__main__":
    import argparse
    
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(
        description="Convert MLVU test annotations to standardized format."
    )
    parser.add_argument("--hf_root", type=str, required=True)
    parser.add_argument("--data_root", type=str, default="./dataset")
    args = parser.parse_args()
    process_data(args)

# CI systems.  For each variable, some CI systems that use the variable
# are indicated.  The collection was chosen so that for each of a number
# of popular systems, at least one of the environment variables is used.
# This list is used to provide some indication of and lower bound for
# CI traffic to PyPI.  Thus, it is okay if the list is not comprehensive.
# For more background, see: https://github.com/pypa/pip/issues/5499
CI_ENVIRONMENT_VARIABLES = (
    # Azure Pipelines
    "BUILD_BUILDID",
    # Jenkins
    "BUILD_ID",
    # AppVeyor, CircleCI, Codeship, Gitlab CI, Shippable, Travis CI
    "CI",
    # Explicit environment variable.
    "PIP_IS_CI",
)
def appears_as_ci() -> bool:
    """
    Return whether it looks like pip is running under CI.
    """
    # We don't use the method of checking for a tty (e.g. using isatty())
    # because some CI systems mimic a tty (e.g. Travis CI).  Thus that
    # method doesn't provide definitive information in either direction.
    return any(name in os.environ for name in CI_ENVIRONMENT_VARIABLES)
def user_agent() -> str:
    """
    Return a string representing the user agent.
    """
    info: Dict[str, Any] = {
        "installer": {"name": "pip", "version": __version__},
        "python": platform.python_version(),
        "implementation": {
            "name": platform.python_implementation(),
        },
    }
    if info["implementation"]["name"] == "CPython":
        info["implementation"]["version"] = platform.python_version()
    elif info["implementation"]["name"] == "PyPy":
        pypy_version_info = sys.pypy_version_info  # type: ignore
        if pypy_version_info.releaselevel == "final":
            pypy_version_info = pypy_version_info[:3]
        info["implementation"]["version"] = ".".join(
            [str(x) for x in pypy_version_info]
        )
    elif info["implementation"]["name"] == "Jython":
        # Complete Guess
        info["implementation"]["version"] = platform.python_version()
    elif info["implementation"]["name"] == "IronPython":
        # Complete Guess
        info["implementation"]["version"] = platform.python_version()
    if sys.platform.startswith("linux"):
        from pip._vendor import distro
        linux_distribution = distro.name(), distro.version(), distro.codename()
        distro_infos: Dict[str, Any] = dict(
            filter(
                lambda x: x[1],
                zip(["name", "version", "id"], linux_distribution),
            )
        )
        libc = dict(
            filter(
                lambda x: x[1],
                zip(["lib", "version"], libc_ver()),
            )
        )
        if libc:
            distro_infos["libc"] = libc
        if distro_infos:
            info["distro"] = distro_infos
    if sys.platform.startswith("darwin") and platform.mac_ver()[0]:
        info["distro"] = {"name": "macOS", "version": platform.mac_ver()[0]}
    if platform.system():
        info.setdefault("system", {})["name"] = platform.system()
    if platform.release():
        info.setdefault("system", {})["release"] = platform.release()
    if platform.machine():
        info["cpu"] = platform.machine()
    if has_tls():
        import _ssl as ssl
        info["openssl_version"] = ssl.OPENSSL_VERSION
    setuptools_dist = get_default_environment().get_distribution("setuptools")
    if setuptools_dist is not None:
        info["setuptools_version"] = str(setuptools_dist.version)
    if shutil.which("rustc") is not None:
        # If for any reason `rustc --version` fails, silently ignore it
        try:
            rustc_output = subprocess.check_output(
                ["rustc", "--version"], stderr=subprocess.STDOUT, timeout=0.5
            )
        except Exception:
            pass
        else:
            if rustc_output.startswith(b"rustc "):
                # The format of `rustc --version` is:
                # `b'rustc 1.52.1 (9bc8c42bb 2021-05-09)\n'`
                # We extract just the middle (1.52.1) part
                info["rustc_version"] = rustc_output.split(b" ")[1].decode()
    # Use None rather than False so as not to give the impression that
    # pip knows it is not being run under CI.  Rather, it is a null or
    # inconclusive result.  Also, we include some value rather than no
    # value to make it easier to know that the check has been run.
    info["ci"] = True if appears_as_ci() else None
    user_data = os.environ.get("PIP_USER_AGENT_USER_DATA")
    if user_data is not None:
        info["user_data"] = user_data
    return "{data[installer][name]}/{data[installer][version]} {json}".format(
        data=info,
        json=json.dumps(info, separators=(",", ":"), sort_keys=True),
    )
class LocalFSAdapter(BaseAdapter):
    def send(
        self,
        request: PreparedRequest,
        stream: bool = False,
        timeout: Optional[Union[float, Tuple[float, float]]] = None,
        verify: Union[bool, str] = True,
        cert: Optional[Union[str, Tuple[str, str]]] = None,
        proxies: Optional[Mapping[str, str]] = None,
    ) -> Response:
        pathname = url_to_path(request.url)
        resp = Response()
        resp.status_code = 200
        resp.url = request.url
        try:
            stats = os.stat(pathname)
        except OSError as exc:
            # format the exception raised as a io.BytesIO object,
            # to return a better error message:
            resp.status_code = 404
            resp.reason = type(exc).__name__
            resp.raw = io.BytesIO(f"{resp.reason}: {exc}".encode("utf8"))
        else:
            modified = email.utils.formatdate(stats.st_mtime, usegmt=True)
            content_type = mimetypes.guess_type(pathname)[0] or "text/plain"
            resp.headers = CaseInsensitiveDict(
                {
                    "Content-Type": content_type,
                    "Content-Length": stats.st_size,
                    "Last-Modified": modified,
                }
            )
            resp.raw = open(pathname, "rb")
            resp.close = resp.raw.close
        return resp
    def close(self) -> None:
        pass
class _SSLContextAdapterMixin:
    """Mixin to add the ``ssl_context`` constructor argument to HTTP adapters.
    The additional argument is forwarded directly to the pool manager. This allows us
    to dynamically decide what SSL store to use at runtime, which is used to implement
    the optional ``truststore`` backend.
    """
    def __init__(
        self,
        *,
        ssl_context: Optional["SSLContext"] = None,
        **kwargs: Any,
    ) -> None:
        self._ssl_context = ssl_context
        super().__init__(**kwargs)
    def init_poolmanager(
        self,
        connections: int,
        maxsize: int,
        block: bool = DEFAULT_POOLBLOCK,
        **pool_kwargs: Any,
    ) -> "PoolManager":
        if self._ssl_context is not None:
            pool_kwargs.setdefault("ssl_context", self._ssl_context)
        return super().init_poolmanager(  # type: ignore[misc]
            connections=connections,
            maxsize=maxsize,
            block=block,
            **pool_kwargs,
        )

class PipSession(requests.Session):
    timeout: Optional[int] = None
    def __init__(
        self,
        *args: Any,
        retries: int = 0,
        cache: Optional[str] = None,
        trusted_hosts: Sequence[str] = (),
        index_urls: Optional[List[str]] = None,
        ssl_context: Optional["SSLContext"] = None,
        **kwargs: Any,
    ) -> None:
        """
        :param trusted_hosts: Domains not to emit warnings for when not using
            HTTPS.
        """
        super().__init__(*args, **kwargs)
        # Namespace the attribute with "pip_" just in case to prevent
        # possible conflicts with the base class.
        self.pip_trusted_origins: List[Tuple[str, Optional[int]]] = []
        # Attach our User Agent to the request
        self.headers["User-Agent"] = user_agent()
        # Attach our Authentication handler to the session
        self.auth = MultiDomainBasicAuth(index_urls=index_urls)
        # Create our urllib3.Retry instance which will allow us to customize
        # how we handle retries.
        retries = urllib3.Retry(
            # Set the total number of retries that a particular request can
            # have.
            total=retries,
            # A 503 error from PyPI typically means that the Fastly -> Origin
            # connection got interrupted in some way. A 503 error in general
            # is typically considered a transient error so we'll go ahead and
            # retry it.
            # A 500 may indicate transient error in Amazon S3
            # A 502 may be a transient error from a CDN like CloudFlare or CloudFront
            # A 520 or 527 - may indicate transient error in CloudFlare
            status_forcelist=[500, 502, 503, 520, 527],
            # Add a small amount of back off between failed requests in
            # order to prevent hammering the service.
            backoff_factor=0.25,
        )  # type: ignore
        # Our Insecure HTTPAdapter disables HTTPS validation. It does not
        # support caching so we'll use it for all http:// URLs.
        # If caching is disabled, we will also use it for
        # https:// hosts that we've marked as ignoring
        # TLS errors for (trusted-hosts).
        insecure_adapter = InsecureHTTPAdapter(max_retries=retries)
        # We want to _only_ cache responses on securely fetched origins or when
        # the host is specified as trusted. We do this because
        # we can't validate the response of an insecurely/untrusted fetched
        # origin, and we don't want someone to be able to poison the cache and
        # require manual eviction from the cache to fix it.
        if cache:
            secure_adapter = CacheControlAdapter(
                cache=SafeFileCache(cache),
                max_retries=retries,
                ssl_context=ssl_context,
            )
            self._trusted_host_adapter = InsecureCacheControlAdapter(
                cache=SafeFileCache(cache),
                max_retries=retries,
            )
        else:
            secure_adapter = HTTPAdapter(max_retries=retries, ssl_context=ssl_context)
            self._trusted_host_adapter = insecure_adapter
        self.mount("https://", secure_adapter)
        self.mount("http://", insecure_adapter)
        # Enable file:// urls
        self.mount("file://", LocalFSAdapter())
        for host in trusted_hosts:
            self.add_trusted_host(host, suppress_logging=True)
    def update_index_urls(self, new_index_urls: List[str]) -> None:
        """
        :param new_index_urls: New index urls to update the authentication
            handler with.
        """
        self.auth.index_urls = new_index_urls
    def add_trusted_host(
        self, host: str, source: Optional[str] = None, suppress_logging: bool = False
    ) -> None:
        """
        :param host: It is okay to provide a host that has previously been
            added.
        :param source: An optional source string, for logging where the host
            string came from.
        """
        if not suppress_logging:
            msg = f"adding trusted host: {host!r}"
            if source is not None:
                msg += f" (from {source})"
            logger.info(msg)
        parsed_host, parsed_port = parse_netloc(host)
        if parsed_host is None:
            raise ValueError(f"Trusted host URL must include a host part: {host!r}")
        if (parsed_host, parsed_port) not in self.pip_trusted_origins:
            self.pip_trusted_origins.append((parsed_host, parsed_port))
        self.mount(
            build_url_from_netloc(host, scheme="http") + "/", self._trusted_host_adapter
        )
        self.mount(build_url_from_netloc(host) + "/", self._trusted_host_adapter)
        if not parsed_port:
            self.mount(
                build_url_from_netloc(host, scheme="http") + ":",
                self._trusted_host_adapter,
            )
            # Mount wildcard ports for the same host.
            self.mount(build_url_from_netloc(host) + ":", self._trusted_host_adapter)
    def iter_secure_origins(self) -> Generator[SecureOrigin, None, None]:
        yield from SECURE_ORIGINS
        for host, port in self.pip_trusted_origins:
            yield ("*", host, "*" if port is None else port)
    def is_secure_origin(self, location: Link) -> bool:
        # Determine if this url used a secure transport mechanism
        parsed = urllib.parse.urlparse(str(location))
        origin_protocol, origin_host, origin_port = (
            parsed.scheme,
            parsed.hostname,
            parsed.port,
        )
        # The protocol to use to see if the protocol matches.
        # Don't count the repository type as part of the protocol: in
        # cases such as "git+ssh", only use "ssh". (I.e., Only verify against
        # the last scheme.)
        origin_protocol = origin_protocol.rsplit("+", 1)[-1]
        # Determine if our origin is a secure origin by looking through our
        # hardcoded list of secure origins, as well as any additional ones
        # configured on this PackageFinder instance.
        for secure_origin in self.iter_secure_origins():
            secure_protocol, secure_host, secure_port = secure_origin
            if origin_protocol != secure_protocol and secure_protocol != "*":
                continue
            try:
                addr = ipaddress.ip_address(origin_host or "")
                network = ipaddress.ip_network(secure_host)
            except ValueError:
                # We don't have both a valid address or a valid network, so
                # we'll check this origin against hostnames.
                if (
                    origin_host
                    and origin_host.lower() != secure_host.lower()
                    and secure_host != "*"
                ):
                    continue
            else:
                # We have a valid address and network, so see if the address
                # is contained within the network.
                if addr not in network:
                    continue
            # Check to see if the port matches.
            if (
                origin_port != secure_port
                and secure_port != "*"
                and secure_port is not None
            ):
                continue
            # If we've gotten here, then this origin matches the current
            # secure origin and we should return True
            return True
        # If we've gotten to this point, then the origin isn't secure and we
        # will not accept it as a valid location to search. We will however
        # log a warning that we are ignoring it.
        logger.warning(
            "The repository located at %s is not a trusted or secure host and "
            "is being ignored. If this repository is available via HTTPS we "
            "recommend you use HTTPS instead, otherwise you may silence "
            "this warning and allow it anyway with '--trusted-host %s'.",
            origin_host,
            origin_host,
        )
        return False
    def request(self, method: str, url: str, *args: Any, **kwargs: Any) -> Response:
        # Allow setting a default timeout on a session
        kwargs.setdefault("timeout", self.timeout)
        # Allow setting a default proxies on a session
        kwargs.setdefault("proxies", self.proxies)
        # Dispatch the actual request
        return super().request(method, url, *args, **kwargs)

# Migration script for database schema updates using Alembic
import os
import sys
from logging.config import fileConfig
from sqlalchemy import engine_from_config, pool
from alembic import context

# Add parent directory to path to access DB models
sys.path.append(os.path.join(os.path.dirname(__file__), ".."))
from db.schema import Base

# Alembic configuration object containing .ini file settings
alembic_config = context.config

# Configure Python logging based on the config file
if alembic_config.config_file_name is not None:
    fileConfig(alembic_config.config_file_name)

# Attach model metadata for autogenerate support
target_metadata = Base.metadata

# Additional config values can be retrieved as needed
# example_option = alembic_config.get_main_option("example_option")

def run_migrations_offline() -> None:
    """Execute migrations in offline mode.
    
    In this mode, only a database URL is required; no Engine object is created.
    This avoids needing a live DBAPI connection during migration execution.
    """
    db_url = alembic_config.get_main_option("sqlalchemy.url")
    context.configure(
        url=db_url,
        target_metadata=target_metadata,
        literal_binds=True,
        dialect_opts={"paramstyle": "named"},
        render_as_batch=True,
    )
    context.execute("PRAGMA foreign_keys=ON")  # Enable foreign key constraints for SQLite
    with context.begin_transaction():
        context.run_migrations()

def run_migrations_online() -> None:
    """Execute migrations in online mode.
    
    In this mode, an Engine is created and connected to the context
    for direct database interaction.
    """
    connectable = engine_from_config(
        alembic_config.get_section(alembic_config.config_ini_section, {}),
        prefix="sqlalchemy.",
        poolclass=pool.NullPool,
    )
    
    with connectable.connect() as connection:
        context.configure(
            connection=connection,
            target_metadata=target_metadata,
            render_as_batch=True,
        )
        context.execute("PRAGMA foreign_keys=ON")  # Enable foreign key constraints for SQLite
        with context.begin_transaction():
            context.run_migrations()

# Determine execution mode and run appropriate migration function
if context.is_offline_mode():
    run_migrations_offline()
else:
    run_migrations_online()

# Calculate the greatest common divisor using Euclidean algorithm
def gcd(x: int, y: int) -> int:
    """ Return the greatest common divisor of two integers x and y
    >>> gcd(3, 5)
    1
    >>> gcd(25, 15)
    5
    """
    x = abs(x)
    y = abs(y)
    while y:
        x, y = y, x % y
    return x

from typing import Any, Dict, Tuple, Optional, Literal

class FocusMode(Enum):
    """Available attention modes"""
    FIXED_GRID = "fixed_tiles"      # Fixed-size grid tiles (3x4)
    MOVING_BOX = "dynamic_box"      # Dynamic bounding box
    AUTO_SELECT = "adaptive"        # Automatically choose based on scene


class FocusStatus(Enum):
    """Current focus state"""
    IDLE_STATE = "idle"
    TRACKING_MODE = "tracking"
    ACTIVE_PROCESS = "processing"


@dataclass
class TargetRegion:
    """Represents current target region"""
    left: int       # Top-left x
    top: int        # Top-left y 
    w: int          # Region width
    h: int          # Region height
    certitude: float
    status: FocusStatus
    mode: FocusMode
    latent_vec: Optional[np.ndarray] = None
    

class AttentionMechanism(ABC):
    """Base class for attention mechanisms"""
    
    @abstractmethod
    def determine_target(self, movement_map: np.ndarray, current_target: Optional[TargetRegion]) -> TargetRegion:
        """Determine target region from movement map"""
        pass
    
    @abstractmethod
    def get_initial_target(self, img_width: int, img_height: int) -> TargetRegion:
        """Get default/idle target region"""
        pass


class GridBasedMechanism(AttentionMechanism):
    """Fixed-size tile grid mechanism (like hierarchical_attention_gravity)"""
    
    def __init__(self, cols=8, rows=8, target_cols=4, target_rows=3):
        self.grid_cols = cols
        self.grid_rows = rows
        self.target_cols = target_cols
        self.target_rows = target_rows
        self.gravity_factor = 0.6
        
        # Fractional position for smooth movement
        self.fcx = (cols - target_cols) / 2
        self.fcy = (rows - target_rows) / 2
        
    def determine_target(self, movement_map: np.ndarray, current_target: Optional[TargetRegion]) -> TargetRegion:
        """Determine target using tile-based gravity"""
        height, width = movement_map.shape
        tile_h = height // self.grid_rows
        tile_w = width // self.grid_cols
        
        # Compute tile scores
        tile_scores = np.zeros((self.grid_rows, self.grid_cols))
        for r in range(self.grid_rows):
            for c in range(self.grid_cols):
                r1, r2 = r * tile_h, (r + 1) * tile_h
                c1, c2 = c * tile_w, (c + 1) * tile_w
                tile_scores[r, c] = np.mean(movement_map[r1:r2, c1:c2])
        
        # Find max motion tile
        max_movement = np.max(tile_scores)
        
        if max_movement > 0.1:  # Motion threshold - more sensitive
            max_r, max_c = np.unravel_index(np.argmax(tile_scores), tile_scores.shape)
            
            # Update fractional position with gravity
            target_c = max(0, min(self.grid_cols - self.target_cols, max_c - self.target_cols // 2))
            target_r = max(0, min(self.grid_rows - self.target_rows, max_r - self.target_rows // 2))
            
            self.fcx += self.gravity_factor * (target_c - self.fcx)
            self.fcy += self.gravity_factor * (target_r - self.fcy)
            
            status = FocusStatus.ACTIVE_PROCESS if max_movement > 0.3 else FocusStatus.TRACKING_MODE
        else:
            # Return to center
            center_c = (self.grid_cols - self.target_cols) / 2
            center_r = (self.grid_rows - self.target_rows) / 2
            self.fcx += 0.1 * (center_c - self.fcx)
            self.fcy += 0.1 * (center_r - self.fcy)
            status = FocusStatus.IDLE_STATE
        
        # Convert to pixel coordinates
        tile_c = round(self.fcx)
        tile_r = round(self.fcy)
        
        return TargetRegion(
            left=tile_c * tile_w,
            top=tile_r * tile_h,
            w=self.target_cols * tile_w,
            h=self.target_rows * tile_h,
            certitude=max_movement,
            status=status,
            mode=FocusMode.FIXED_GRID
        )
    
    def get_initial_target(self, img_width: int, img_height: int) -> TargetRegion:
        """Get centered target"""
        tile_h = img_height // self.grid_rows
        tile_w = img_width // self.grid_cols
        center_c = (self.grid_cols - self.target_cols) // 2
        center_r = (self.grid_rows - self.target_rows) // 2
        
        return TargetRegion(
            left=center_c * tile_w,
            top=center_r * tile_h,
            w=self.target_cols * tile_w,
            h=self.target_rows * tile_h,
            certitude=0.0,
            status=FocusStatus.IDLE_STATE,
            mode=FocusMode.FIXED_GRID
        )


class AdaptiveBoxMechanism(AttentionMechanism):
    """Dynamic bounding box mechanism (like fast_camera_monitor)"""
    
    def __init__(self, smoothing=0.7, min_dimension=64, max_dimension=320):
        self.smoothing = smoothing
        self.min_dimension = min_dimension
        self.max_dimension = max_dimension
        self.previous_box = None
        self.warmup_frames = 30  # Skip first frames
        
    def determine_target(self, movement_map: np.ndarray, current_target: Optional[TargetRegion]) -> TargetRegion:
        """Compute dynamic bounding box around movement"""
        height, width = movement_map.shape
        
        # Use higher threshold to filter out noise
        movement_threshold = 0.3  # Much higher to ignore camera noise
        
        # Find strongest movement point instead of all movement
        max_movement = np.max(movement_map)
        
        if max_movement > movement_threshold:
            # Find peak movement location
            r_peak, c_peak = np.unravel_index(np.argmax(movement_map), movement_map.shape)
            
            # Calculate box size based on movement spread
            # Find all significant movement points
            movement_points = np.where(movement_map > movement_threshold * 0.5)
            
            if len(movement_points[0]) > 0:
                # Calculate spread of movement
                r_min, r_max = np.min(movement_points[0]), np.max(movement_points[0])
                c_min, c_max = np.min(movement_points[1]), np.max(movement_points[1])
                
                # Box size based on movement spread
                spread_w = c_max - c_min
                spread_h = r_max - r_min
                
                # Adaptive size with limits
                box_size = max(self.min_dimension, 
                              min(self.max_dimension, 
                                  int(max(spread_w, spread_h) * 1.5)))
            else:
                box_size = 128  # Default
            
            half_size = box_size // 2
            
            c = max(0, c_peak - half_size)
            r = max(0, r_peak - half_size)
            w = min(box_size, width - c)
            h = min(box_size, height - r)
            
            # Smooth transitions if we have previous position
            if current_target and self.previous_box:
                alpha = self.smoothing
                prev_c, prev_r, prev_w, prev_h = self.previous_box
                c = int(prev_c * alpha + c * (1 - alpha))
                r = int(prev_r * alpha + r * (1 - alpha))
                w = int(prev_w * alpha + w * (1 - alpha))
                h = int(prev_h * alpha + h * (1 - alpha))
            
            self.previous_box = (c, r, w, h)
            
            return TargetRegion(
                left=c, top=r, w=w, h=h,
                certitude=max_movement,
                status=FocusStatus.ACTIVE_PROCESS if max_movement > 0.5 else FocusStatus.TRACKING_MODE,
                mode=FocusMode.MOVING_BOX
            )
        else:
            # No significant movement - maintain position or center
            if self.previous_box:
                # Keep last position but mark as idle
                c, r, w, h = self.previous_box
                return TargetRegion(
                    left=c, top=r, w=w, h=h,
                    certitude=0.0,
                    status=FocusStatus.IDLE_STATE,
                    mode=FocusMode.MOVING_BOX
                )
            else:
                # Return to center with default size
                default_size = 128
                return TargetRegion(
                    left=(width - default_size) // 2,
                    top=(height - default_size) // 2,
                    w=default_size,
                    h=default_size,
                    certitude=0.0,
                    status=FocusStatus.IDLE_STATE,
                    mode=FocusMode.MOVING_BOX
                )
    
    def get_initial_target(self, img_width: int, img_height: int) -> TargetRegion:
        """Get centered box"""
        size = 128
        return TargetRegion(
            left=(img_width - size) // 2,
            top=(img_height - size) // 2,
            w=size,
            h=size,
            certitude=0.0,
            status=FocusStatus.IDLE_STATE,
            mode=FocusMode.MOVING_BOX
        )


class VisualFocusPlugin(IRPPlugin):
    """
    Single-sensor vision plugin with adaptive attention mechanisms
    """
    
    def __init__(self, 
                 sensor_id: int = 0,
                 mode: FocusMode = FocusMode.AUTO_SELECT,
                 use_vae: bool = True,
                 vae_threshold: float = 0.5,
                 device: Optional[torch.device] = None):
        """
        Initialize visual focus plugin for a single sensor
        
        Args:
            sensor_id: Camera/sensor ID
            mode: Attention mode to use
            use_vae: Whether to use VAE processing
            vae_threshold: Movement threshold to trigger VAE
            device: Torch device for computation
        """
        # Create config for base class
        config = {
            'entity_id': f'vision_sensor_{sensor_id}',
            'max_iterations': 1,  # Vision is single-pass
            'device': str(device),
            'trust_weight': 1.0
        }
        super().__init__(config)
        
        self.sensor_id = sensor_id
        self.device = device or torch.device('cuda' if torch.cuda.is_available() else 'cpu')
        self.use_vae = use_vae
        self.vae_threshold = vae_threshold
        
        # Attention mechanisms
        self.grid_mechanism = GridBasedMechanism()
        self.adaptive_mechanism = AdaptiveBoxMechanism()
        self.current_mode = mode
        
        # Select initial mechanism
        if mode == FocusMode.FIXED_GRID:
            self.mechanism_impl = self.grid_mechanism
        elif mode == FocusMode.MOVING_BOX:
            self.mechanism_impl = self.adaptive_mechanism
        else:  # AUTO_SELECT
            self.mechanism_impl = self.grid_mechanism  # Start with fixed
        
        # Current state
        self.target_region = None
        self.prev_gray = None
        self.movement_history = []
        
        # VAE (lazy loaded)
        self.vae = None
        self.vae_loaded = False
        self.vae_last_used = 0
        self.vae_timeout = 5.0
        
        # Performance tracking
        self.frame_count = 0
        self.vae_inference_time = 0
        self.total_processing_time = 0
        
    def load_vae_model(self):
        """Lazy load VAE model"""
        if not self.vae_loaded and self.use_vae:
            self.vae = TinyVAE(input_channels=3, latent_dim=16, img_size=64)
            self.vae = self.vae.to(self.device)
            self.vae.eval()
            self.vae_loaded = True
            self.vae_last_used = time.time()
            print(f"VAE loaded for sensor {self.sensor_id}")
    
    def unload_vae_model(self):
        """Unload VAE to save memory"""
        if self.vae_loaded:
            del self.vae
            self.vae = None
            self.vae_loaded = False
            if torch.cuda.is_available():
                torch.cuda.empty_cache()
            print(f"VAE unloaded for sensor {self.sensor_id}")
    
    def calculate_movement(self, frame: np.ndarray) -> np.ndarray:
        """Compute movement map from frame"""
        gray = cv2.cvtColor(frame, cv2.COLOR_BGR2GRAY)
        gray = cv2.GaussianBlur(gray, (5, 5), 0)
        
        if self.prev_gray is None:
            self.prev_gray = gray
            return np.zeros_like(gray, dtype=np.float32)
        
        # Movement detection
        diff = cv2.absdiff(self.prev_gray, gray)
        
        # Debug: check raw diff values
        max_diff = np.max(diff)
        mean_diff = np.mean(diff)
        
        # Don't use sigmoid - it might be squashing values too much
        # Just normalize to 0-1
        movement = diff.astype(np.float32) / 255.0
        
        # Optional: amplify weak movement
        movement = np.minimum(movement * 2.0, 1.0)
        
        self.prev_gray = gray
        return movement
    
    def change_mode(self, mode: FocusMode):
        """Switch attention mode"""
        self.current_mode = mode
        
        if mode == FocusMode.FIXED_GRID:
            self.mechanism_impl = self.grid_mechanism
        elif mode == FocusMode.MOVING_BOX:
            self.mechanism_impl = self.adaptive_mechanism
        else:  # AUTO_SELECT
            # Choose based on scene characteristics
            # For now, default to fixed
            self.mechanism_impl = self.grid_mechanism
    
    def get_crop(self, frame: np.ndarray, region: TargetRegion, size: int = 64) -> np.ndarray:
        """Extract crop from target region"""
        # Get center of region
        cx = region.left + region.w // 2
        cy = region.top + region.h // 2
        
        # Extract crop
        half = size // 2
        x1 = max(0, cx - half)
        y1 = max(0, cy - half)
        x2 = min(frame.shape[1], x1 + size)
        y2 = min(frame.shape[0], y1 + size)
        
        crop = frame[y1:y2, x1:x2]
        
        # Resize if needed
        if crop.shape[0] != size or crop.shape[1] != size:
            crop = cv2.resize(crop, (size, size))
        
        return crop
    
    def process_with_vae(self, crop: np.ndarray) -> Tuple[np.ndarray, np.ndarray]:
        """Process crop through VAE"""
        self.load_vae_model()
        self.vae_last_used = time.time()
        
        # Convert to tensor
        crop_tensor = torch.from_numpy(crop).float() / 255.0
        crop_tensor = crop_tensor.permute(2, 0, 1).unsqueeze(0)
        crop_tensor = crop_tensor.to(self.device)
        
        # VAE forward pass
        start_time = time.time()
        with torch.no_grad():
            mu, logvar = self.vae.encode(crop_tensor)
            latent = self.vae.reparameterize(mu, logvar)
            reconstruction = self.vae.decode(latent)
        self.vae_inference_time = time.time() - start_time
        
        # Convert back
        latent_np = latent.cpu().numpy().squeeze()
        recon_np = reconstruction.cpu().numpy().squeeze()
        recon_np = np.transpose(recon_np, (1, 2, 0))
        recon_np = (recon_np * 255).astype(np.uint8)
        
        return latent_np, recon_np
    
    def refine(self, input_data: Any, max_iterations: int = 5) -> Tuple[Any, Dict[str, Any]]:
        """
        Main IRP refinement - process single frame
        
        Args:
            input_data: Frame from camera (numpy array)
            max_iterations: Not used for vision (single pass)
            
        Returns:
            Tuple of (target_region, telemetry)
        """
        start_time = time.time()
        
        # Ensure we have a frame
        if not isinstance(input_data, np.ndarray):
            return None, {"error": "Invalid input"}
        
        frame = input_data
        self.frame_count += 1
        
        # Compute movement map
        movement = self.calculate_movement(frame)
        
        # Get target region from mechanism
        if self.target_region is None:
            self.target_region = self.mechanism_impl.get_initial_target(
                frame.shape[1], frame.shape[0]
            )
        
        self.target_region = self.mechanism_impl.determine_target(movement, self.target_region)
        
        # Adaptive mode switching
        if self.current_mode == FocusMode.AUTO_SELECT:
            # Simple heuristic: use dynamic for high movement variance
            movement_variance = np.var(movement)
            if movement_variance > 0.1 and isinstance(self.mechanism_impl, GridBasedMechanism):
                self.change_mode(FocusMode.MOVING_BOX)
            elif movement_variance < 0.05 and isinstance(self.mechanism_impl, AdaptiveBoxMechanism):
                self.change_mode(FocusMode.FIXED_GRID)
        
        # VAE processing if enabled and movement detected
        latent = None
        reconstruction = None
        if self.use_vae and self.target_region.certitude > self.vae_threshold:
            crop = self.get_crop(frame, self.target_region)
            latent, reconstruction = self.process_with_vae(crop)
            self.target_region.latent_vec = latent
        
        # Check VAE timeout
        if self.vae_loaded and (time.time() - self.vae_last_used) > self.vae_timeout:
            self.unload_vae_model()
        
        # Build telemetry
        self.total_processing_time = time.time() - start_time
        
        telemetry = {
            "sensor_id": self.sensor_id,
            "frame": self.frame_count,
            "focus_x": self.target_region.left,
            "focus_y": self.target_region.top,
            "focus_width": self.target_region.w,
            "focus_height": self.target_region.h,
            "confidence": self.target_region.certitude,
            "state": self.target_region.status.value,
            "strategy": self.target_region.mode.value,
            "vae_loaded": self.vae_loaded,
            "vae_time_ms": self.vae_inference_time * 1000,
            "total_time_ms": self.total_processing_time * 1000,
            "has_latent": latent is not None
        }
        
        # Return target region and telemetry
        return self.target_region, telemetry
    
    def get_state(self) -> Dict[str, Any]:
        """Get plugin state"""
        return {
            "sensor_id": self.sensor_id,
            "strategy": self.current_mode.value,
            "vae_enabled": self.use_vae,
            "vae_loaded": self.vae_loaded,
            "frame_count": self.frame_count,
            "focus": {
                "x": self.target_region.left if self.target_region else 0,
                "y": self.target_region.top if self.target_region else 0,
                "width": self.target_region.w if self.target_region else 0,
                "height": self.target_region.h if self.target_region else 0,
                "confidence": self.target_region.certitude if self.target_region else 0.0
            }
        }
    
    def trust_adjustment(self) -> float:
        """Compute trust based on consistency"""
        # Higher trust when focus is stable and confident
        if self.target_region and self.target_region.status == FocusStatus.ACTIVE_PROCESS:
            return 0.9  # High trust when actively processing
        elif self.target_region and self.target_region.status == FocusStatus.TRACKING_MODE:
            return 0.7  # Medium trust when tracking
        else:
            return 0.5  # Lower trust when idle
    
    def shutdown(self):
        """Cleanup on shutdown"""
        if self.vae_loaded:
            self.unload_vae_model()


def create_visual_focus_plugin(
    sensor_id: int = 0,
    mode: str = "adaptive",
    use_vae: bool = True,
    device: Optional[torch.device] = None
) -> VisualFocusPlugin:
    """
    Factory function to create visual focus plugin
    
    Args:
        sensor_id: Camera/sensor ID
        mode: "fixed_tiles", "dynamic_box", or "adaptive"
        use_vae: Whether to enable VAE processing
        device: Torch device
        
    Returns:
        Configured VisualFocusPlugin instance
    """
    mode_map = {
        "fixed_tiles": FocusMode.FIXED_GRID,
        "dynamic_box": FocusMode.MOVING_BOX,
        "adaptive": FocusMode.AUTO_SELECT
    }
    
    mode_enum = mode_map.get(mode, FocusMode.AUTO_SELECT)
    
    return VisualFocusPlugin(
        sensor_id=sensor_id,
        mode=mode_enum,
        use_vae=use_vae,
        device=device
    )

    source: str,
    target: str,
    fixture_id: str,
    layer: str,
) -> str | None:
    """Return a reason string if this cross-format combo is a known limitation, else None."""
    # thinking response: openai:cli doesn't support ThinkingBlock in non-streaming
    if fixture_id == "thinking" and layer == "cross_response":
        if source in _THINKING_RESPONSE_LOSSY_SOURCES:
            return f"{source} does not parse thinking content into ThinkingBlock"
        if target in _THINKING_RESPONSE_LOSSY_TARGETS:
            return f"{target} does not preserve ThinkingBlock in non-streaming responses"
    return None

# Shared pattern database for AI Agent Security skill suite.
# Central registry of detection patterns derived from research notes 01-09
# and examples 01-04. Used by vet-repo, scan-skill, and audit-code skills.
"""
import re
from dataclasses import dataclass, field
from enum import Enum
from typing import Optional

class Severity(Enum):
    CRITICAL = "CRITICAL"
    HIGH = "HIGH"
    MEDIUM = "MEDIUM"
    LOW = "LOW"
    INFO = "INFO"

class Category(Enum):
    SKILL_INJECTION = "skill_injection"
    HOOK_ABUSE = "hook_abuse"
    MCP_CONFIG = "mcp_config"
    SECRETS = "secrets"
    DANGEROUS_CALLS = "dangerous_calls"
    EXFILTRATION = "exfiltration"
    ENCODING_OBFUSCATION = "encoding_obfuscation"
    INSTRUCTION_OVERRIDE = "instruction_override"
    SUPPLY_CHAIN = "supply_chain"
    FILE_PERMISSIONS = "file_permissions"

@dataclass
class Pattern:
    name: str
    regex_pattern: str
    severity_level: Severity
    description_text: str
    category_type: Category
    compiled_regex: Optional[re.Pattern] = field(default=None, repr=False)
    
    def __post_init__(self) -> None:
        self.compiled_regex = re.compile(self.regex_pattern, re.IGNORECASE)

@dataclass
class Finding:
    pattern_name: str
    severity_level: Severity
    category_type: Category
