VOCAB_FILES_NAMES = {"vocab_file": "vocab.txt"}

def load_vocab(vocab_file):
    """Loads a vocabulary file into a dictionary."""
    vocab = collections.OrderedDict()
    with open(vocab_file, "r", encoding="utf-8") as reader:
        tokens = reader.readlines()
    for idx, token in enumerate(tokens):
        token = token.rstrip("\n")
        vocab[token] = idx
    return vocab

def whitespace_tokenize(text):
    """Runs basic whitespace cleaning and splitting on a piece of text."""
    text = text.strip()
    if not text:
        return []
    tokens = text.split()
    return tokens

class DistilBertTokenizer(PreTrainedTokenizer):
    r"""
    Construct a DistilBERT tokenizer. Based on WordPiece.
    This tokenizer inherits from [`PreTrainedTokenizer`] which contains most of the main methods. Users should refer to
    this superclass for more information regarding those methods.
    Args:
        vocab_file (`str`):
            File containing the vocabulary.
        do_lower_case (`bool`, *optional*, defaults to `True`):
            Whether or not to lowercase the input when tokenizing.
        do_basic_tokenize (`bool`, *optional*, defaults to `True`):
            Whether or not to do basic tokenization before WordPiece.
        never_split (`Iterable`, *optional*):
            Collection of tokens which will never be split during tokenization. Only has an effect when
            `do_basic_tokenize=True`
        unk_token (`str`, *optional*, defaults to `"[UNK]"`):
            The unknown token. A token that is not in the vocabulary cannot be converted to an ID and is set to be this
            token instead.
        sep_token (`str`, *optional*, defaults to `"[SEP]"`):
            The separator token, which is used when building a sequence from multiple sequences, e.g. two sequences for
            sequence classification or for a text and a question for question answering. It is also used as the last
            token of a sequence built with special tokens.
        pad_token (`str`, *optional*, defaults to `"[PAD]"`):
            The token used for padding, for example when batching sequences of different lengths.
        cls_token (`str`, *optional*, defaults to `"[CLS]"`):
            The classifier token which is used when doing sequence classification (classification of the whole sequence
            instead of per-token classification). It is the first token of the sequence when built with special tokens.
        mask_token (`str`, *optional*, defaults to `"[MASK]"`):
            The token used for masking values. This is the token used when training this model with masked language
            modeling. This is the token which the model will try to predict.
        tokenize_chinese_chars (`bool`, *optional*, defaults to `True`):
            Whether or not to tokenize Chinese characters.
            This should likely be deactivated for Japanese (see this
            [issue](https://github.com/huggingface/transformers/issues/328)).
        strip_accents (`bool`, *optional*):
            Whether or not to strip all accents. If this option is not specified, then it will be determined by the
            value for `lowercase` (as in the original BERT).
    """
    vocab_files_names = VOCAB_FILES_NAMES
    model_input_names = ["input_ids", "attention_mask"]
    
    def __init__(
        self,
        vocab_file,
        do_lower_case=True,
        do_basic_tokenize=True,
        never_split=None,
        unk_token="[UNK]",
        sep_token="[SEP]",
        pad_token="[PAD]",
        cls_token="[CLS]",
        mask_token="[MASK]",
        tokenize_chinese_chars=True,
        strip_accents=None,
        **kwargs,
    ):
        if not os.path.isfile(vocab_file):
            raise ValueError(
                f"Can't find a vocabulary file at path '{vocab_file}'. To load the vocabulary from a Google pretrained"
                " model use `tokenizer = DistilBertTokenizer.from_pretrained(PRETRAINED_MODEL_NAME)`"
            )
        self.vocab = load_vocab(vocab_file)
        self.ids_to_tokens = collections.OrderedDict([(idx, tok) for tok, idx in self.vocab.items()])
        self.do_basic_tokenize = do_basic_tokenize
        
        if do_basic_tokenize:
            self.basic_tokenizer = BasicTokenizer(
                do_lower_case=do_lower_case,
                never_split=never_split,
                tokenize_chinese_chars=tokenize_chinese_chars,
                strip_accents=strip_accents,
            )
            
        self.wordpiece_tokenizer = WordpieceTokenizer(vocab=self.vocab, unk_token=str(unk_token))
        
        super().__init__(
            do_lower_case=do_lower_case,
            do_basic_tokenize=do_basic_tokenize,
            never_split=never_split,
            unk_token=unk_token,
            sep_token=sep_token,
            pad_token=pad_token,
            cls_token=cls_token,
            mask_token=mask_token,
            tokenize_chinese_chars=tokenize_chinese_chars,
            strip_accents=strip_accents,
            **kwargs,
        )

    @property
    def do_lower_case(self):
        return self.basic_tokenizer.do_lower_case

    @property
    def vocab_size(self):
        return len(self.vocab)

    def get_vocab(self):
        return dict(self.vocab, **self.added_tokens_encoder)

    def _tokenize(self, text, split_special_tokens=False):
        split_tokens = []
        if self.do_basic_tokenize:
            for token in self.basic_tokenizer.tokenize(

def generate_class(name: str, implementation: str) -> str:
    """
    Generate a class definition for an activation function.
    
    Parameters
    ----------
    name : str
        Name of the activation function class.
    implementation : str
        Full path to the underlying JAX function.
        
    Returns
    -------
    str
        Complete class definition as a string.
    """
    return f"""
@jaxtyped(typechecker=beartype)
class {name}(ActivationBase):
    \"\"\"
    Elementwise activation function for ``{implementation}``.
    See Also
    --------
    {implementation} : The function used for the elementwise activation.
    \"\"\"
    def __init__(self, *args, **kwargs):
        self.args = args
        self.kwargs = kwargs
        super().__init__(*args, **kwargs)
    def func(self, x: jax.numpy.ndarray) -> jax.numpy.ndarray:
        return {implementation}(x, *self.args, **self.kwargs)
"""

import os
import contextlib
import tempfile
import shutil
import logging
import time
import random
from typing import Generator, Any

logger = logging.getLogger(__name__)

# Retry configuration parameters
MAX_ATTEMPTS = 5
INITIAL_WAIT = 0.1  # seconds

@contextlib.contextmanager
def safe_file_write(
    target_path: str, 
    open_mode: str = "w", 
    text_encoding: str = "utf-8", 
    **extra_kwargs: Any
) -> Generator[Any, None, None]:
    """
    Context manager for safely writing files atomically.
    
    Writes to a temporary file in the same directory, then performs an atomic
    rename operation to the final destination. Ensures data integrity using fsync.
    
    Args:
        target_path: Destination file path
        open_mode: File opening mode (default 'w')
        text_encoding: Character encoding for text mode (default 'utf-8')
        **extra_kwargs: Additional parameters passed to open()
        
    Yields:
        File object for writing operations
    """
    # Determine directory and filename components
    dir_path = os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(target_path))
    file_name = os.path.basename(target_path)
    
    # Ensure parent directory exists
    if dir_path and not os.path.exists(dir_path):
        os.makedirs(dir_path, exist_ok=True)
        
    # Create temporary file with unique name
    # delete=False needed because we manage closing manually before renaming
    # prefix pattern helps identify temp files during debugging
    temp_prefix = f".{file_name}_"
    fd, temp_file_path = tempfile.mkstemp(
        dir=dir_path, 
        prefix=temp_prefix, 
        suffix=".tmp", 
        text="b" not in open_mode
    )
    
    file_obj = None
    try:
        # Wrap file descriptor with Python file object
        file_obj = os.fdopen(
            fd, 
            open_mode, 
            encoding=text_encoding if "b" not in open_mode else None, 
            **extra_kwargs
        )
        
        # Provide file handle to caller
        yield file_obj
        
        # Push buffered data to OS
        file_obj.flush()
        
        # Force OS to commit data to disk
        os.fsync(file_obj.fileno())
        
        # Close file before moving it
        file_obj.close()
        file_obj = None  # Avoid double-close in exception handler
        
        # Preserve original file permissions if target already exists
        if os.path.exists(target_path):
            try:
                shutil.copystat(target_path, temp_file_path)
            except OSError as perm_error:
                logger.warning(f"Unable to copy permissions for {target_path}: {perm_error}")
        
        # Perform atomic replacement with retry mechanism
        _perform_atomic_rename(temp_file_path, target_path)
            
    except Exception as write_error:
        # Cleanup on failure
        if file_obj:
            try:
                file_obj.close()
            except Exception:
                pass
        
        # Remove temporary file if it still exists
        if os.path.exists(temp_file_path):
            try:
                os.unlink(temp_file_path)
            except OSError as cleanup_exception:
                logger.warning(f"Cleanup failed for temp file {temp_file_path}: {cleanup_exception}")
                
        raise write_error

def _perform_atomic_rename(source: str, destination: str) -> None:
    """
    Attempt to move source file to destination with retries for lock contention.
    
    Handles transient file locks common on Windows systems by implementing
    exponential backoff with jitter.
    """
    latest_exception = None
    
    for trial in range(MAX_ATTEMPTS):
        try:
            # Use os.replace for atomic operation across platforms
            os.replace(source, destination)
            return
        except OSError as lock_error:
            latest_exception = lock_error
            # Common Windows error codes for file access conflicts
            # 13: Access denied, 32: Sharing violation
            logger.debug(
                f"Rename attempt {trial + 1}/{MAX_ATTEMPTS} failed: {lock_error}"
            )
            
            # Apply increasing delay with random jitter
            wait_time = INITIAL_WAIT * (trial + 1) + (random.random() * 0.1)
            time.sleep(wait_time)
            
    # Exhausted all retries - raise final error
    raise OSError(
        f"Atomic rename of {destination} failed after {MAX_ATTEMPTS} attempts. "
        f"Final error was: {latest_exception}"
    ) from latest_exception

import numpy as np

class SimulationScenario:
    def __init__(self, display, config):
        # Initialize simulation parameters
        self.frames_per_second = config.fps
        self.time_per_frame = 1.0 / self.frames_per_second
        
        # Simulation time tracking
        self.current_time = 0.0
        self.substeps_per_frame = config.substeps
        self.time_step_size = self.time_per_frame / self.substeps_per_frame
        
        # Store viewer reference
        self.display = display
        
        # Build model
        model_builder = newton.ModelBuilder()
        
        # Register custom MPM attributes
        SolverImplicitMPM.register_custom_attributes(model_builder)
        
        # Add particles using static method
        SimulationScenario.spawn_particles(model_builder, config)
        
        # Setup collision objects
        self.collision_object = config.collider
        if self.collision_object == "concave":
            dimensions = (1.0, 2.0, 0.25)
            left_transform = wp.transform(
                wp.vec3(-0.7, 0.0, 0.8), wp.quat_from_axis_angle(wp.vec3(0.0, 1.0, 0.0), np.pi / 4.0)
            )
            right_transform = wp.transform(
                wp.vec3(0.7, 0.0, 0.8), wp.quat_from_axis_angle(wp.vec3(0.0, 1.0, 0.0), -np.pi / 4.0)
            )
            model_builder.add_shape_box(
                body=-1,
                cfg=newton.ModelBuilder.ShapeConfig(mu=0.1, density=0.0),
                xform=left_transform,
                hx=dimensions[0],
                hy=dimensions[1],
                hz=dimensions[2],
            )
            model_builder.add_shape_box(
                body=-1,
                cfg=newton.ModelBuilder.ShapeConfig(mu=0.1, density=0.0),
                xform=right_transform,
                hx=dimensions[0],
                hy=dimensions[1],
                hz=dimensions[2],
            )
        elif self.collision_object != "none":
            box_dimensions = (0.5, 2.0, 0.8)
            if self.collision_object == "cube":
                transform = wp.transform(wp.vec3(0.75, 0.0, 0.8), wp.quat_identity())
            elif self.collision_object == "wedge":
                transform = wp.transform(
                    wp.vec3(0.0, 0.0, 0.9), wp.quat_from_axis_angle(wp.vec3(0.0, 1.0, 0.0), np.pi / 4.0)
                )
            model_builder.add_shape_box(
                body=-1,
                cfg=newton.ModelBuilder.ShapeConfig(mu=0.1),
                xform=transform,
                hx=box_dimensions[0],
                hy=box_dimensions[1],
                hz=box_dimensions[2],
            )
        
        # Add ground plane
        model_builder.add_ground_plane(cfg=newton.ModelBuilder.ShapeConfig(mu=0.5))
        
        # Finalize model and set gravity
        self.physics_model = model_builder.finalize()
        self.physics_model.set_gravity(config.gravity)
        
        # Configure MPM solver options
        mpm_config = SolverImplicitMPM.Config()
        for param_name in vars(config):
            if hasattr(mpm_config, param_name):
                setattr(mpm_config, param_name, getattr(config, param_name))
            if hasattr(self.physics_model.mpm, param_name):
                getattr(self.physics_model.mpm, param_name).fill_(getattr(config, param_name))
        
        # Initialize states
        self.state_initial = self.physics_model.state()
        self.state_next = self.physics_model.state()
        
        # Create solver
        self.solver = SolverImplicitMPM(self.physics_model, mpm_config)
        self.display.set_model(self.physics_model)
        
        # Setup UI callback if using GL viewer
        if isinstance(self.display, newton.viewer.ViewerGL):
            self.display.register_ui_callback(self.draw_ui, position="side")
        
        # Visualization settings
        self.display.show_particles = True
        self.display_normals = False
        self.capture_graph()

    def capture_graph(self):
        self.execution_graph = None
        if wp.get_device().is_cuda and self.solver.grid_type == "fixed":
            if self.substeps_per_frame % 2 != 0:
                wp.utils.warn("Sim substeps must be even for graph capture of MPM step")
            else:
                with wp.ScopedCapture() as capture:
                    self.run_simulation()
                self.execution_graph = capture.graph

    def run_simulation(self):
        for _ in range(self.substeps_per_frame):
            self.solver.step(self.state_initial, self.state_next, None, None, self.time_step_size)
            self.solver._project_outside(self.state_next, self.state_next, self.time_step_size)
            self.state_initial, self.state_next = self.state_next, self.state_initial

    def advance(self):
        if self.execution_graph:
            wp.capture_launch(self.execution_graph)
        else:
            self.run_simulation()
        self.current_time += self.time_per_frame

    def verify_final_state(self):
        voxel_resolution = self.solver.voxel_size
        newton.examples.test_particle_state(
            self.state_initial,
            "all particles are above the ground",
            lambda q, qd: q[2] > -voxel_resolution,

            cube_half_extents = wp.vec3(0.5, 2.0, 0.6) * 0.9
            cube_position = wp.vec3(0.75, 0, 0.9)

            cube_max = cube_position + cube_half_extents
            newton.examples.test_particle_state(
                self.state_initial,
                "all particles are outside the cube",
                lambda q, qd: not newton.math.vec_inside_limits(q, cube_min, cube_max),
            )

    @staticmethod
    def spawn_particles(builder: newton.ModelBuilder, config):
        particle_density = config.density
        grid_spacing = config.voxel_size
        particles_per_cell = 3
        
        # Calculate particle grid dimensions
        min_pos = np.array(config.emit_lo)
        max_pos = np.array(config.emit_hi)
        resolution = np.array(
            np.ceil(particles_per_cell * (max_pos - min_pos) / grid_spacing),
            dtype=int,
        )
        
        cell_dimensions = (max_pos - min_pos) / resolution
        cell_volume = np.prod(cell_dimensions)
        particle_radius = np.max(cell_dimensions) * 0.5
        particle_mass = cell_volume * particle_density
        
        builder.add_particle_grid(
            pos=wp.vec3(min_pos),
            rot=wp.quat_identity(),
            vel=wp.vec3(0.0),
            dim_x=resolution[0] + 1,
            dim_y=resolution[1] + 1,
            dim_z=resolution[2] + 1,
            cell_x=cell_dimensions[0],
            cell_y=cell_dimensions[1],
            cell_z=cell_dimensions[2],
            mass=particle_mass,
            jitter=2.0 * particle_radius,
            radius_mean=particle_radius,
        )

class DataCollatorForInternvl(object):
    def __init__(self, padding_token_id, **kwargs):
        self.padding_token_id = padding_token_id
        self.ignore_value = MODEL_CONSTANTS['internvl']['IGNORE_INDEX']
    
    def __call__(self, sample_batch):
        first_item = sample_batch[0]
        result_batch = {}
        sequence_lengths = [item["input_ids"].shape for item in sample_batch]
        max_sequence_length = max(sequence_lengths)[0]
        
        for item in sample_batch:
            padded_input_ids = torch.LongTensor([self.padding_token_id] * max_sequence_length)
            padded_input_ids[:item["input_ids"].shape[0]] = item["input_ids"]
            item["input_ids"] = padded_input_ids
            
            padded_labels = torch.LongTensor([self.ignore_value] * max_sequence_length)
            padded_labels[:item["labels"].shape[0]] = item["labels"]
            item["labels"] = padded_labels
            
            item["attention_mask"] = item["input_ids"].ne(self.padding_token_id)
        
        # Handle labels specifically
        if "label" in first_item and first_item["label"] is not None:
            label_value = first_item["label"].item() if isinstance(first_item["label"], torch.Tensor) else first_item["label"]
            dtype = torch.long if isinstance(label_value, int) else torch.float
            result_batch["labels"] = torch.tensor([item["label"] for item in sample_batch], dtype=dtype)
        elif "label_ids" in first_item and first_item["label_ids"] is not None:
            if isinstance(first_item["label_ids"], torch.Tensor):
                result_batch["labels"] = torch.stack([item["label_ids"] for item in sample_batch])
            else:
                dtype = torch.long if isinstance(first_item["label_ids"][0], int) else torch.float
                result_batch["labels"] = torch.tensor([item["label_ids"] for item in sample_batch], dtype=dtype)
        
        # Process remaining keys
        for key, value in first_item.items():
            if key not in ("label", "label_ids", "pixel_values", "image_flags") and \
                    value is not None and not isinstance(value, str):
                if isinstance(value, torch.Tensor):
                    result_batch[key] = torch.stack([item[key] for item in sample_batch])
                elif isinstance(value, np.ndarray):
                    result_batch[key] = torch.tensor(np.stack([item[key] for item in sample_batch]))
                else:
                    result_batch[key] = torch.tensor([item[key] for item in sample_batch])
            
            if key in ("pixel_values", "image_flags"):
                if isinstance(value, torch.Tensor):
                    result_batch[key] = torch.concat([item[key] for item in sample_batch])
                elif isinstance(value, np.ndarray):
                    result_batch[key] = torch.concat(torch.tensor(np.stack([item[key] for item in sample_batch])))
                else:
                    result_batch[key] = torch.concat([item[key] for item in sample_batch])
        
        return result_batch


class DataCollatorForDeepSeekVL(object):
    def __init__(self, padding_token_id, **kwargs):
        self.padding_token_id = padding_token_id
        self.masking_id = MODEL_CONSTANTS["deepseekvl2"]["IGNORE_INDEX"]
    
    def __call__(self, example_list):
        batched_input_sequences = [sample["input_ids"] for sample in example_list]
        batched_target_sequences = [sample["labels"] for sample in example_list]
        batched_image_masks = [sample["images_seq_mask"] for sample in example_list]
        sequence_lengths = [len(sample) for sample in example_list]
        
        # Pad sequences
        batched_input_sequences = pad_sequence(batched_input_sequences, batch_first=True, padding_value=self.padding_token_id)
        batched_target_sequences = pad_sequence(batched_target_sequences, batch_first=True, padding_value=self.masking_id)
        batched_image_masks = pad_sequence(batched_image_masks, batch_first=True, padding_value=0)
        batched_attention_masks = batched_input_sequences != self.padding_token_id
        
        # Pad images to maximum patch number
        max_patch_count = max(sample["images"].shape[0] for sample in example_list)
        batched_images = []
        for sample in example_list:
            images = sample["images"]
            pad_count = max_patch_count - images.shape[0]
            if pad_count > 0:
                padding_tensor = torch.zeros((pad_count, *images.shape[1:]), dtype=images.dtype)
                images = torch.cat([images, padding_tensor], dim=0)
            batched_images.append(images)
        batched_images = torch.stack(batched_images, dim=0)
        
        # Pad spatial crop information
        max_image_count = max(sample["images_spatial_crop"].shape[0] for sample in example_list)
        batched_spatial_crops = []
        for sample in example_list:
            spatial_crop = sample["images_spatial_crop"]
            crop_pad_count = max_image_count - sample["images_spatial_crop"].shape[0]
            if crop_pad_count > 0:
                crop_padding = torch.full((crop_pad_count, 2), 0, dtype=spatial_crop.dtype)
                spatial_crop = torch.cat([spatial_crop, crop_padding], dim=0)
            batched_spatial_crops.append(spatial_crop)
        batched_spatial_crops = torch.stack(batched_spatial_crops, dim=0)
        
        return {
            "input_ids": batched_input_sequences,
            "labels": batched_target_sequences,
            "attention_mask": batched_attention_masks,
            "images": batched_images,
            "images_seq_mask": batched_image_masks,
            "images_spatial_crop": batched_spatial_crops
        }


@dataclass
class DataCollatorSpeechSeq2SeqWithPadding:
    def __init__(self, processor_path, target_language, processing_task, **kwargs):
        self.processor = WhisperProcessor.from_pretrained(
            processor_path,
            language=target_language,
            task=processing_task,
            local_files_only=True,
        )
    
    def __call__(
            self, samples: List[Dict[str, Union[List[int], torch.Tensor]]]
    ) -> Dict[str, torch.Tensor]:
        # Separate audio inputs and labels due to different length requirements
        audio_features = [
            {"input_features": sample["input_features"]}
            for sample in samples
        ]
        audio_batch = self.processor.feature_extractor.pad(
            audio_features, return_tensors="pt"
        )
        
        # Tokenize labels
        label_features = [{"input_ids": sample["labels"]} for sample in samples]
        labels_batch = self.processor.tokenizer.pad(label_features, return_tensors="pt")
        
        # Replace padding tokens to ignore loss
        labels = labels_batch["input_ids"].masked_fill(
            labels_batch.attention_mask.ne(1), -100
        )
        
        # Remove bos token if present
        if (labels[:, 0] == self.processor.tokenizer.bos_token_id).all().cpu().item():
            labels = labels[:, 1:]
        
        audio_batch["labels"] = labels
        return audio_batch

class DataCollatorForOpenSoraPlan:
    def __init__(
            self,
            batch_size: int = 1,
            num_frames: int = 13,
            group_by_frame: bool = False,
            group_by_resolution: bool = False,
            group_by_data: bool = False,
            max_height: int = 480,
            max_width: int = 640,
            vae_scale_factor: Tuple[int] = (4, 8, 8),
            use_video_representation: bool = False,
            use_text_representation: bool = False,
            **kwargs
    ):
        self.batch_size = batch_size
        self.group_by_frame = group_by_frame
        self.group_by_resolution = group_by_resolution
        self.group_by_data = group_by_data
        self.max_height = max_height
        self.max_width = max_width
        
        predictor_model_config = get_value_from_args("mm.model.predictor")
        patch_size_thw = predictor_model_config.patch_size_thw
        self.patch_h = patch_size_thw[1]
        self.patch_t = patch_size_thw[0]
        self.vae_stride_h = vae_scale_factor[1]
        self.vae_stride_t = vae_scale_factor[0]
        self.vae_stride_whole = vae_scale_factor
        self.num_frames = num_frames
        self.max_temporal_spatial = (self.num_frames, self.max_height, self.max_width)
        self.use_video_representation = use_video_representation
        self.use_text_representation = use_text_representation
    
    @staticmethod
    def package(batch):
        batch_tubes = [i.get(VIDEO, None) for i in batch]  # b [c t h w]
        file_info = [i.get(FILE_INFO, None) for i in batch]
        if not isinstance(batch[0].get(PROMPT_IDS, None), list):
            input_ids = [i.get(PROMPT_IDS, None) for i in batch]  # b [1 l]
            cond_mask = [i.get(PROMPT_MASK, None) for i in batch]  # b [1 l]
        else:
            input_ids = list(map(list, zip(*[i[PROMPT_IDS] for i in batch])))
            cond_mask = list(map(list, zip(*[i[PROMPT_MASK] for i in batch])))
        return batch_tubes, input_ids, cond_mask, file_info
    
    @staticmethod
    def validate_prompt_shape(prompt_ids, is_list):
        if not is_list:
            if prompt_ids.dim() != 2 and prompt_ids.dim() != 3:
                raise ValueError(
                    f"prompt shape must have dim 2 for non featured data or 3 for featured data, but got {prompt_ids.dim()}")
        else:
            if prompt_ids[0].dim() != 2 and prompt_ids[0].dim() != 3:
                raise ValueError(
                    f"prompt shape must have dim 2 for non featured data or 3 for featured data, but got {prompt_ids.dim()}")
    
    def package_features(self, batch):
        is_list = isinstance(batch[0].get(PROMPT_IDS, None), list)
        for item in batch:
            if item.get(VIDEO).dim() != 4:
                raise ValueError(f"video shape must have dim 4, but got {item.get(VIDEO).dim()}")
            if item.get(PROMPT_MASK, None) and item.get(PROMPT_MASK).dim() != 2:
                raise ValueError(
                    f"prompt mask must be None or have dim 2 for non featured and featured data, but got {item.get(PROMPT_MASK).dim()}")
            if item.get(VIDEO_MASK, None) and item.get(VIDEO_MASK).dim() != 3:
                raise ValueError(f"video_mask shape must be None or have dim 3, but got {item.get(VIDEO_MASK).dim()}")
            prompt_ids = item.get(PROMPT_IDS)
            self.validate_prompt_shape(prompt_ids, is_list)
        
        batch_tubes = [item.get(VIDEO, None) for item in batch]
        video_mask = [item.get(VIDEO_MASK, None) for item in batch]
        if all([i is None or not any(i) for i in video_mask]):
            video_mask = None
        
        if not is_list:
            input_ids = [item.get(PROMPT_IDS, None) for item in batch]  # b [1 l]
            cond_mask = [item.get(PROMPT_MASK, None) for item in batch]  # b [1 l]
        elif self.use_text_representation:
            input_ids = [item.get(PROMPT_IDS, None)[0] for item in batch]  # b [1 l]
            cond_mask = [item.get(PROMPT_MASK, None)[0] for item in batch]  # b [1
            warnings.warn("input_ids_2 and cond_mask_2 features are not supported yet and will be None for now",
                          FutureWarning)
        else:
            input_ids = list(map(list, zip(*[item[PROMPT_IDS] for item in batch])))
            cond_mask = list(map(list, zip(*[item[PROMPT_MASK] for item in batch])))
        return batch_tubes, video_mask, input_ids, cond_mask
    
    def __call__(self, batch):
        if not self.use_video_representation:
            batch_tubes, input_ids, cond_mask, file_info = self.package(batch)
            temporal_stride = self.vae_stride_t * self.patch_t
            spatial_stride = self.vae_stride_h * self.patch_h
            processed_data = self.process(
                batch_tubes,
                input_ids,
                cond_mask,
                temporal_stride,
                spatial_stride,
                self.max_temporal_spatial,
                self.vae_stride_whole,
            )
            if torch.any(torch.isnan(processed_data.padded_batch_tubes)):
                raise AssertionError("after pad_batch_tubes.")
            return {
                VIDEO: processed_data.padded_batch_tubes,
                PROMPT_IDS: processed_data.input_ids,
                VIDEO_MASK: processed_data.attention_mask,
                PROMPT_MASK: processed_data.cond_mask,
                MASKED_VIDEO: processed_data.masked_video,
                INPUT_MASK: processed_data.input_mask,
                FILE_INFO: file_info
            }
        else:
            batch_tubes, video_mask, input_ids, cond_mask = self.package_features(batch)
            if not isinstance(input_ids[0], list):
                input_ids = torch.stack(input_ids)  # b 1 l
                cond_mask = torch.stack(cond_mask)  # b 1 l
            else:
                input_ids = [
                    torch.stack(_input_ids)  # b 1 l
                    for _input_ids in input_ids
                ]
                cond_mask = [
                    torch.stack(_cond_mask)  # b 1 l
                    for _cond_mask in cond_mask
                ]
            return {
                VIDEO: torch.stack(batch_tubes),
                PROMPT_IDS: input_ids,
                VIDEO_MASK: torch.stack(video_mask) if video_mask else None,
                PROMPT_MASK: cond_mask,
                MASKED_VIDEO: None,
                INPUT_MASK: None,
            }
    
    def process(
        self,
        batch_tubes,
        input_ids,
        cond_mask,
        t_ds_stride,
        ds_stride,
        max_thw,
        ae_stride_thw,
    ):
        # pad to max multiple of ds_stride
        batch_input_size = [i.shape for i in batch_tubes]  # [(c t h w), (c t h w)]
        if len(batch_input_size) != self.batch_size:
            raise AssertionError("batch_input_size and batch_size are not equal.")
        
        is_grouped = self.group_by_frame or self.group_by_resolution or self.group_by_data or self.batch_size == 1
        if is_grouped:  #
            len_each_batch = batch_input_size
            idx_length_dict = dict([*zip(list(range(self.batch_size)), len_each_batch)])
            count_dict = Counter(len_each_batch)
            if len(count_dict) != 1:
                sorted_by_value = sorted(count_dict.items(), key=lambda item: item[1])
                pick_length = sorted_by_value[-1][0]  # the highest frequency
                candidate_batch = [
                    idx
                    for idx, length in idx_length_dict.items()
                    if length == pick_length
                ]
                random_select_batch = [
                    random.choice(candidate_batch)
                    for _ in range(len(len_each_batch) - len(candidate_batch))
                ]
                print(
                    batch_input_size,
                    idx_length_dict,
                    count_dict,
                    sorted_by_value,
                    pick_length,
                    candidate_batch,
                    random_select_batch,
                )
                pick_idx = candidate_batch + random_select_batch
                batch_tubes = [batch_tubes[i] for i in pick_idx]
                batch_input_size = [
                    i.shape
                    for i in batch_tubes
                ]  # [(c t h w), (c t h w)]
                if not isinstance(input_ids[0], list):
                    input_ids = [input_ids[i] for i in pick_idx]  # b [1, l]
                    cond_mask = [cond_mask[i] for i in pick_idx]  # b [1, l]
                else:
                    input_ids = [
                        [_input_ids[i] for i in pick_idx]  # b [1, l]
                        for _input_ids in input_ids
                    ]
                    cond_mask = [
                        [_cond_mask[i] for i in pick_idx]  # b [1, l]
                        for _cond_mask in cond_mask
                    ]
            for i in range(1, self.batch_size):
                if batch_input_size[0] != batch_input_size[i]:
                    raise AssertionError(
                        f"batch_input_size{0} and batch_input_size{i} are not equal."
                    )
                max_t = max([i[1] for i in batch_input_size])
                max_h = max([i[2] for i in batch_input_size])
                max_w = max([i[3] for i in batch_input_size])
        else:
            max_t, max_h, max_w = max_thw
        
        pad_max_t, pad_max_h, pad_max_w = (
            self.pad_to_multiple(max_t - 1 + self.vae_stride_t, t_ds_stride),
            self.pad_to_multiple(max_h, ds_stride),
            self.pad_to_multiple(max_w, ds_stride),
        )
        pad_max_t = pad_max_t + 1 - self.vae_stride_t
        
        each_pad_t_h_w = [
            [pad_max_t - i.shape[1], pad_max_h - i.shape[2], pad_max_w - i.shape[3]]
            for i in batch_tubes
        ]
        pad_batch_tubes = [
            F.pad(im, (0, pad_w, 0, pad_h, 0, pad_t), value=0)
            for (pad_t, pad_h, pad_w), im in zip(each_pad_t_h_w, batch_tubes)
        ]
        pad_batch_tubes = torch.stack(pad_batch_tubes, dim=0)
        
        max_tube_size = [pad_max_t, pad_max_h, pad_max_w]
        max_latent_size = [
            ((max_tube_size[0] - 1) // ae_stride_thw[0] + 1),
            max_tube_size[1] // ae_stride_thw[1],
            max_tube_size[2] // ae_stride_thw[2],
        ]
        valid_latent_size = [
            [
                int(math.ceil((i[1] - 1) / ae_stride_thw[0])) + 1,
                int(math.ceil(i[2] / ae_stride_thw[1])),
                int(math.ceil(i[3] / ae_stride_thw[2])),
            ]
            for i in batch_input_size
        ]
        attention_mask = [
            F.pad(
                torch.ones(i, dtype=pad_batch_tubes.dtype),
                (
                    0,
                    max_latent_size[2] - i[2],
                    0,
                    max_latent_size[1] - i[1],
                    0,
                    max_latent_size[0] - i[0],
                ),
                value=0,
            )
            for i in valid_latent_size
        ]
        attention_mask = torch.stack(attention_mask)  # b t h w
        
        if self.batch_size == 1 or self.group_by_frame or self.group_by_resolution:
            if not torch.all(attention_mask.bool()):
                raise AssertionError("All elements of attention_mask are zero")
        
        if not isinstance(input_ids[0], list):
            input_ids = torch.stack(input_ids)  # b 1 l
            cond_mask = torch.stack(cond_mask)  # b 1 l
        else:
            input_ids = [
                torch.stack(_input_ids)  # b 1 l
                for _input_ids in input_ids
            ]
            cond_mask = [
                torch.stack(_cond_mask)  # b 1 l
                for _cond_mask in cond_mask
            ]
        
        # if opensoraplan i2v dataset, batch_tube has masked_video and mask
        if pad_batch_tubes.shape[1] == 7:
            pad_batch_tubes, masked_video, input_mask = pad_batch_tubes[:, :3], pad_batch_tubes[:,
                                                                        3:6], pad_batch_tubes[:, 6:7]
        else:
            masked_video = None
            input_mask = None
        
        processed_data = ProcessedData(pad_batch_tubes, attention_mask, input_ids, cond_mask,
                                      masked_video, input_mask)
        return processed_data
    
    @staticmethod
    def pad_to_multiple(number, ds_stride):
        remainder = number % ds_stride
        if remainder == 0:
            return number
        else:
            padding = ds_stride - remainder
            return number + padding


class ProcessedData:
    def __init__(self, padded_batch_tubes, attention_mask, input_ids, cond_mask, masked_video,
                 input_mask):
        self.padded_batch_tubes = padded_batch_tubes
        self.attention_mask = attention_mask
        self.input_ids = input_ids
        self.cond_mask = cond_mask
        self.masked_video = masked_video
        self.input_mask = input_mask

def _register_handler(handler, file_extensions):
    """Register a handler for specified file extensions.
    
    Args:
        handler (:obj:`BaseFileHandler`): Handler instance to be registered.
        file_extensions (str or list[str]): File extensions to be handled.
    """
    if not isinstance(handler, BaseFileHandler):
        raise TypeError(
            f"handler must inherit from BaseFileHandler, got {type(handler)}"
        )
    
    # Normalize file_extensions to a list
    if isinstance(file_extensions, str):
        file_extensions = [file_extensions]
    
    # Validate all items are strings
    if not all([isinstance(ext, str) for ext in file_extensions]):
        raise TypeError("file_extensions must be a string or list of strings")
    
    # Register each extension with the handler
    for ext in file_extensions:
        handler_registry[ext] = handler


def register_handler(file_extensions, **kwargs):
    """Decorator to register custom handlers."""
    def decorator(cls):
        _register_handler(cls(**kwargs), file_extensions)
        return cls
    return decorator

import enum
from pathlib import Path

class Phase(enum.StrEnum):
    training = enum.auto()
    resume_training = enum.auto()
    predict = enum.auto()

def build_main_parser() -> argparse.ArgumentParser:
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(allow_abbrev=False)
    subparsers = parser.add_subparsers(dest="phase")
    
    train_parser = subparsers.add_parser(
        Phase.training,
        help="Start training a WeatherGenerator model from scratch.",
    )
    _append_train_arguments(train_parser)
    
    resume_parser = subparsers.add_parser(
        Phase.resume_training,
        help="Continue training an existing WeatherGenerator model.",
    )
    _append_resume_arguments(resume_parser)
    
    predict_parser = subparsers.add_parser(
        Phase.predict,
        help="Perform prediction using a trained WeatherGenerator model",
    )
    _append_predict_arguments(predict_parser)
    
    return parser

def build_training_parser() -> argparse.ArgumentParser:
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(allow_abbrev=False)
    _append_train_arguments(parser)
    return parser

def build_resume_parser() -> argparse.ArgumentParser:
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(allow_abbrev=False)
    _append_resume_arguments(parser)
    return parser

def build_predict_parser() -> argparse.ArgumentParser:
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(allow_abbrev=False)
    _append_predict_arguments(parser)
    return parser

def _append_train_arguments(parser: argparse.ArgumentParser):
    _append_common_arguments(parser)

def _append_resume_arguments(parser: argparse.ArgumentParser):
    _append_common_arguments(parser)
    _append_model_loading_options(parser)
    parser.add_argument(
        "--finetune-forecast",
        action="store_true",
        help=(
            "Fine-tune for forecasting. This overrides certain Config settings. "
            "Settings specified via --config take priority."
        ),
    )

def _append_predict_arguments(parser: argparse.ArgumentParser):
    _append_model_loading_options(parser)
    _append_common_arguments(parser)
    
    parser.add_argument(
        "--start-date",
        "-start",
        type=_parse_date_string,
        default="2022-10-01",
        help="Inference start date. Must be parseable by pd.to_datetime.",
    )
    
    parser.add_argument(
        "--end-date",
        "-end",
        type=_parse_date_string,
        default="2022-12-01",
        help="Inference end date. Must be parseable by pd.to_datetime.",
    )
    
    parser.add_argument(
        "--samples", type=int, default=5000000, help="Number of samples to generate during inference."
    )
    
    parser.add_argument(  # behavior modified => implies default=False
        "--save-samples",
        type=bool,
        default=True,
        help="Enable or disable saving of inference samples. Default is True.",
    )
    
    parser.add_argument(
        "--output-streams",
        nargs="+",
        help="Specify output streams for inference.",
    )

def _parse_date_string(date_str: str) -> str:
    try:
        parsed = pd.to_datetime(date_str, errors="raise")
    except (pd.errors.ParserError, ValueError) as e:
        msg = f"Invalid date format in input '{date_str}' (type: {type(date_str)})."
        raise ValueError(msg) from e
    return parsed.strftime("%Y%m%d%H%M")

def _append_common_arguments(parser: argparse.ArgumentParser):
    parser.add_argument(
        "--private-config",
        type=Path,
        default=None,
        help=(
            "Path to the private configuration file containing platform-specific details "
            "such as directory paths."
        ),
    )
    
    parser.add_argument(
        "--config",
        type=Path,
        nargs="*",
        default=[],
        help="Optional experiment-specific configuration files listed in increasing order of precedence.",
    )
    
    parser.add_argument(
        "--run-id",
        type=str,
        help=(
            "Identifier for this run."
            " All outputs (models, logs, etc.) will be stored under this ID."
            " If omitted, a new unique ID will be generated."
        ),
    )
    
    parser.add_argument(
        "--overrides",
        nargs="+",
        default=[],
        help=(
            "Override specific config parameters."
            " These take precedence over values from --config or --finetune_forecast."
            " Format: parent_obj.nested_obj=value"
        ),
    )
    
    parser.add_argument(
        "--base-config",
        type=Path,
        nargs="?",
        help=(
            "Path to the base configuration file."

        default=None,
    )

def _append_model_loading_options(parser: argparse.ArgumentParser):
    parser.add_argument(
        "-id",
        "--source-run-id",
        required=True,
        help=(
            "Run ID of the pretrained WeatherGenerator model to use "
            "for inference or continued training."
        ),
    )
    
    parser.add_argument(
        "-e",
        "--checkpoint-epoch",
        type=int,
        default=-1,
        help=(
            "Checkpoint epoch of the pretrained model "
            "(Default -1 uses the latest checkpoint)."
        ),
    )
    
    parser.add_argument(
        "--preserve-run-id",
        action="store_true",
        help="Reuse the ID from --source-run-id for the current run. "

# Quota management system supporting per-user and per-service limits
# (typically deployed in cluster environments like OpenShift)
# Each limit is defined by a distinct _quota limiter_ instance, which can be
# either `user_limiter` or `cluster_limiter` (the latter being the naming convention
# used in OpenShift deployments). Every limiter supports three configuration parameters:
# 1. `period` — expressed in human-readable format; refer to
#    https://www.postgresql.org/docs/current/datatype-datetime.html#DATATYPE-INTERVAL-INPUT
#    for accepted formats. Upon period expiration, quota is either reset or incremented.
# 2. `initial_quota` — the starting allowance at the beginning of each period.
# 3. `quota_increase` — optional value added to the quota when a new period starts.
#
# Two common usage patterns:
# 1. Periodic reset to a fixed amount (e.g., weekly or monthly): set `initial_quota`
#    to the desired baseline value.
# 2. Periodic increment by a fixed amount (e.g., daily): specify `quota_increase`.
#
# Technically, both `initial_quota` and `quota_increase` may be specified together.
# In such cases, upon period expiry, the quota is *reset* to `initial_quota + quota_increase`.
#
# Multiple quota limiters can coexist—for instance, one limiter could add 100,000 tokens/day,
# while another resets to 10,000,000 tokens/month.

from abc import ABC, abstractmethod
from typing import Optional
import datetime
import sqlite3
import psycopg2
from log import get_logger
from models.config import SQLiteDatabaseConfiguration, PostgreSQLDatabaseConfiguration
from quota.connect_pg import connect_pg
from quota.connect_sqlite import connect_sqlite

logger = get_logger(__name__)


class QuotaLimiter(ABC):
    """Abstract base class for all quota limiter implementations."""

    @abstractmethod
    def available_quota(self, subject_id: str) -> int:
        """Fetch remaining quota for a given subject.
        
        Args:
            subject_id (str): Unique identifier of the subject (user/service).
            
        Returns:
            int: Number of quota units currently available.
        """

    @abstractmethod
    def revoke_quota(self) -> None:
        """Zero out the current quota for the target subject.
        
        This disables further usage until quota is restored via increase/reset.
        """

    @abstractmethod
    def increase_quota(self) -> None:
        """Apply configured quota increment to the subject's balance.
        
        Updates persistent storage with the incremental addition.
        """

    @abstractmethod
    def ensure_available_quota(self, subject_id: str = "") -> None:
        """Validate that sufficient quota remains for the subject."""

    @abstractmethod
    def consume_tokens(
        self, input_tokens: int, output_tokens: int, subject_id: str = ""
    ) -> None:
        """Deduct token usage from subject's quota.
        
        Args:
            input_tokens (int): Input token count to subtract.
            output_tokens (int): Output token count to subtract.
            subject_id (str): Subject whose quota is reduced; defaults to default subject.
        """

    @abstractmethod
    def __init__(self) -> None:
        """Construct a QuotaLimiter instance and configure database connections.
        
        Attributes:
            sqlite_connection_config (Optional[SQLiteDatabaseConfiguration]):
                SQLite config, or `None` if not configured.
            postgres_connection_config (Optional[PostgreSQLDatabaseConfiguration]):
                PostgreSQL config, or `None` if not configured.
        """
        self.sqlite_connection_config: Optional[SQLiteDatabaseConfiguration] = None
        self.postgres_connection_config: Optional[PostgreSQLDatabaseConfiguration] = (
            None
        )

    @abstractmethod
    def _initialize_tables(self) -> None:
        """Set up required database schema and indexes.
        
        Must be idempotent—safe to call repeatedly. Raises exception on failure.
        """

    # pylint: disable=W0201
    def connect(self) -> None:
        """Establish database connection and initialize storage.
        
        Connects to configured backend (PostgreSQL or SQLite), initializes tables,
        and enables autocommit. On initialization failure, closes connection and re-raises.
        """
        logger.info("Initializing connection to quota limiter database")
        if self.postgres_connection_config is not None:
            self.connection = connect_pg(self.postgres_connection_config)
        if self.sqlite_connection_config is not None:
            self.connection = connect_sqlite(self.sqlite_connection_config)
            # Python 3.12+ deprecates default adapters; use custom ones instead.
            sqlite3.register_adapter(
                datetime.datetime, lambda val: val.replace(tzinfo=None).isoformat()
            )
        try:
            self._initialize_tables()
        except Exception as e:
            self.connection.close()
            logger.exception("Error initializing quota limiter database:\n%s", e)
            raise
        self.connection.autocommit = True

    def connected(self) -> bool:
        """Verify active database connection.
        
        Returns:
            bool: `True` if connection is healthy, `False` otherwise.
        """
        if self.connection is None:
            logger.warning("Not connected, will reconnect later")
            return False
        cursor = None
        try:
            cursor = self.connection.cursor()
            cursor.execute("SELECT 1")
            logger.info("Connection to storage is ok")
            return True
        except (psycopg2.OperationalError, sqlite3.Error) as e:
            logger.error("Disconnected from storage: %s", e)
            return False
        finally:
            if cursor is not None:
                try:
                    cursor.close()
                except Exception:  # pylint: disable=broad-exception-caught
                    logger.warning("Unable to close cursor")

@require_vision
class VivitImageProcessingTest(ImageProcessingTestMixin, unittest.TestCase):
    image_processing_class = VivitImageProcessor if is_vision_available() else None

    def setUp(self):
        super().setUp()
        self.image_processor_tester = VivitImageProcessorTester(self)

    @property
    def image_processor_dict(self):
        return self.image_processor_tester.prepare_image_processor_dict()

    def test_image_processor_properties(self):
        processor = self.image_processing_class(**self.image_processor_dict)
        self.assertTrue(hasattr(processor, "image_mean"))
        self.assertTrue(hasattr(processor, "image_std"))
        self.assertTrue(hasattr(processor, "do_normalize"))
        self.assertTrue(hasattr(processor, "do_resize"))
        self.assertTrue(hasattr(processor, "do_center_crop"))
        self.assertTrue(hasattr(processor, "size"))

    def test_image_processor_from_dict_with_kwargs(self):
        processor = self.image_processing_class.from_dict(self.image_processor_dict)
        self.assertEqual(processor.size, {"shortest_edge": 18})
        self.assertEqual(processor.crop_size, {"height": 18, "width": 18})

        processor = self.image_processing_class.from_dict(self.image_processor_dict, size=42, crop_size=84)
        self.assertEqual(processor.size, {"shortest_edge": 42})
        self.assertEqual(processor.crop_size, {"height": 84, "width": 84})

    def test_rescale(self):
        # ViVit optionally rescales between -1 and 1 instead of the usual 0 and 1
        image = np.arange(0, 256, 1, dtype=np.uint8).reshape(1, 8, 32)
        processor = self.image_processing_class(**self.image_processor_dict)

        rescaled_image = processor.rescale(image, scale=1 / 127.5)
        expected_image = (image * (1 / 127.5)).astype(np.float32) - 1
        self.assertTrue(np.allclose(rescaled_image, expected_image))

        rescaled_image = processor.rescale(image, scale=1 / 255, offset=False)
        expected_image = (image / 255.0).astype(np.float32)
        self.assertTrue(np.allclose(rescaled_image, expected_image))

        processor = self.image_processing_class(**self.image_processor_dict)

class _VllmRunner(nn.Module):
    def __init__(self, vllm_model: nn.Module):
        super().__init__()
        self.vllm_model = vllm_model
        has_pooler = is_pooling_model(vllm_model)
        self.pooler = vllm_model.pooler if has_pooler else None
    
    def forward(self, **kwargs) -> th.Tensor:
        if "hidden_state" in kwargs:
            return self.compute_logits(kwargs["hidden_state"])
        else:
            return self.compute_hidden_state(
                kwargs["input_ids"],
                kwargs["positions"],
                kwargs["intermediate_tensors"],
                kwargs["inputs_embeds"],
            )
    
    def compute_hidden_state(
        self,
        input_ids: th.Tensor,
        positions: th.Tensor,
        intermediate_tensors: Optional[IntermediateTensors],
        inputs_embeds: Optional[th.Tensor],
    ) -> th.Tensor:
        hidden_state = self.vllm_model(input_ids, positions,
                                       intermediate_tensors, inputs_embeds)
        return hidden_state
    
    def compute_logits(self, hidden_state: th.Tensor) -> th.Tensor:
        return self.vllm_model.compute_logits(hidden_state)

class VllmModelWrapper:
    """ Wraps a vLLM Pytorch model and let it run on the JAX engine. """
    rng: PRNGK
    mesh: Mesh
    model: _VllmRunner
    
    def __init__(self, vllm_config: VllmConfig, rng: PRNGK, mesh: Mesh):
        self.vllm_config = vllm_config
        self.rng = rng
        self.mesh = mesh
        self.vllm_config.quant_config = get_tpu_quantization_config(
            self.vllm_config, self.mesh)
        self._apply_pp_patch()
        MultiHeadLatentAttentionWrapper.register_oot(
            VllmTPUMultiHeadLatentAttentionWrapper)
    
    def _apply_pp_patch(self):
        # patch `get_pp_group` in vLLM to jax's get_pp_group.
        import sys
        import vllm.distributed as vllm_dist
        import vllm.distributed.parallel_state as vllm_ps
        vllm_ps.get_pp_group = jax_get_pp_group
        vllm_dist.get_pp_group = jax_get_pp_group
        for module_name, module in sys.modules.items():
            if module_name.startswith("vllm.model_executor.models"):
                if hasattr(module, "get_pp_group"):
                    setattr(module, "get_pp_group", jax_get_pp_group)
    
    def load_weights(self):
        loading_start = tm.time()
        # Set up to load the model into CPU first.
        # Cache device slice config since device config cannot be deepcopied
        modified_slice_config = False
        if hasattr(
                self.vllm_config.device_config,
                'slice') and self.vllm_config.device_config.slice is not None:
            slice_config = self.vllm_config.device_config.slice
            modified_slice_config = True
            self.vllm_config.device_config.slice = None
        
        self.vllm_config.compilation_config.static_forward_context.clear()
        vllm_config_for_load = cp.deepcopy(self.vllm_config)
        
        if modified_slice_config:
            self.vllm_config.device_config.slice = slice_config
        
        assert self.vllm_config.model_config.dtype in TORCH_DTYPE_TO_JAX, "The model_config.dtype must be a PyTorch dtype."
        vllm_config_for_load.device_config.device = "cpu"
        
        # Remove the dynamically added sharding_config attribute to avoid errors
        # when vLLM's replace() function checks for dataclass fields.
        # This is safe because vllm_config_for_load is only used for model loading
        # which doesn't need sharding_config, and self.vllm_config still has it.
        if hasattr(vllm_config_for_load, 'sharding_config'):
            delattr(vllm_config_for_load, 'sharding_config')
        
        # Clearing the cached compilation config, otherwise vllm model init will fail
        # When expert parallelism is enabled, vLLM loads weight in sharding
        # aware manner. Since tpu-inference has its own sharding logic, this
        # may casue errors. Therefore, we disable it during weight loading.
        vllm_config_for_load.parallel_config.enable_expert_parallel = False
        
        use_random_weights = (
            vllm_config_for_load.load_config.load_format == "dummy")
        if use_random_weights:
            log.info(
                "Initializing vLLM model with random weights, weight loading skipped."
            )
        
        # The DummyModelLoader in vLLM calls torch._sync for torch_xla path when
        # it detects the tpu platform, but we don't need it and it causes crash
        # without proper setup.
        load_context = ptch(
            "torch._sync",
            return_value=None) if use_random_weights else nc()
        
        # By default load weights to the CPU device first. If we are running
        # under Pathways, this would cause weights to be loaded on a CPU-only
        # node, so we'll need to remove this context.
        jax_context = jx.default_device(
            jx.devices("cpu")
            [0]) if not vllm_envs.VLLM_TPU_USING_PATHWAYS else nc()
        
        # Load the vLLM model and wrap it into a new model whose forward
        # function can calculate the hidden_state and logits.
        with load_context, jax_context:
            vllm_model = vllm_get_model(vllm_config=vllm_config_for_load)
        
        lora_manager = None
        if vllm_config_for_load.lora_config is not None:
            # Replace layers in the model with LoRA layers.
            with thx.default_env():
                # Argument "device" in load_lora_model is used to set the device
                # used in punica wrapper.
                lora_manager, vllm_model = load_lora_model(
                    vllm_model, vllm_config_for_load, device="jax")
            replace_set_lora(vllm_model)
        
        static_forward_context = vllm_config_for_load.compilation_config.static_forward_context
        self.vllm_config.compilation_config.static_forward_context = static_forward_context
        self.vllm_config.compilation_config.static_all_moe_layers = vllm_config_for_load.compilation_config.static_all_moe_layers
        self.model = _VllmRunner(vllm_model)
        params_and_buffers = shard_model_to_tpu(self.model, self.mesh)
        self._pooler: Pooler | None = self.model.pooler
        loading_end = tm.time()
        total_loading_time = loading_end - loading_start
        log.info(
            f"Total time to load model weights from storage to TPU: {total_loading_time:.2f} seconds."
        )
        # Returning to the jax land, so we need to wrap it into a JaxValue.
        return jax_view(params_and_buffers), lora_manager
    
    def jit_step_func(self):
        @jx.jit(
            donate_argnames=("kv_caches", ),
            out_shardings=(
                None,  # kv_caches - keep original sharding
                NamedSharding(self.mesh,
                              PartitionSpec(ShardingAxisName.ATTN_DATA, None)),
                None,  # empty list
            ),
            compiler_options={
                "xla_tpu_all_gather_collective_matmul_mode":
                "post_spmd_conservative",
                "xla_tpu_reduce_scatter_collective_matmul_mode":
                "post_spmd_conservative"
            },
            static_argnames=(
                "layer_name_to_kvcache_index",
                "is_first_rank",
                "is_last_rank",
            ),
        )
        def step_fun(
            params_and_buffers,  # This has been wrapped into torchax TorchValue
            kv_caches: List[jx.Array],
            input_ids: jx.Array,
            attn_metadata: AttentionMetadata,
            input_embeds: jx.Array,
            input_positions: jx.Array,
            layer_name_to_kvcache_index: Seq[Tuple[str, int]],
            lora_metadata,
            intermediate_tensors: JaxIntermediateTensors = None,
            is_first_rank: bool = True,
            is_last_rank: bool = True,
            *args,
        ) -> Tuple[List[jx.Array], jx.Array]:
            layer_name_to_kvcache_index = dict(layer_name_to_kvcache_index)
            lora_metadata = torch_view(lora_metadata)
            with thx.default_env(), set_vllm_model_wrapper_context(
                    kv_caches=kv_caches,
                    mesh=self.mesh,
                    layer_name_to_kvcache_index=layer_name_to_kvcache_index
            ), sfc(attn_metadata=attn_metadata,
                   vllm_config=self.vllm_config):
                # We need to wrap args from jax land into TorchValue with
                # torch_view in order to call the Torch function.
                original_lora_metadata = replace_lora_metadata(
                    self.model, lora_metadata, self.vllm_config.lora_config)
                if not is_first_rank:
                    intermediate_tensors = intermediate_tensors.to_torch()
                output_from_torch = thx.func.functional_call(
                    self.model,
                    torch_view(params_and_buffers),
                    kwargs={
                        "input_ids": torch_view(input_ids),
                        "positions": torch_view(input_positions),
                        "intermediate_tensors": intermediate_tensors,
                        "inputs_embeds": None,
                    },
                    tie_weights=False,
                )
                replace_lora_metadata(self.model, original_lora_metadata,
                                      self.vllm_config.lora_config)
                vllm_model_wrapper_context = get_vllm_model_wrapper_context()
                new_kv_caches = vllm_model_wrapper_context.kv_caches
            
            # Wrap the output(hidden states or intermediate tensor)
            # from torch land into a JaxValue for the jax code to consume.
            if not is_last_rank:
                output = JaxIntermediateTensors.from_torch(output_from_torch)
            else:
                output = jax_view(output_from_torch)
            return new_kv_caches, output, []
        return step_fun
    
    def jit_compute_logits_func(self):
        @jx.jit(out_shardings=(NamedSharding(
            self.mesh,
            PartitionSpec(ShardingAxisName.MLP_DATA,
                          ShardingAxisName.MLP_TENSOR))))
        def compute_logits_func(
            params_and_buffers: Any,
            hidden_states: jx.Array,
            lora_metadata,
        ) -> jx.Array:
            lora_metadata = torch_view(lora_metadata)
            with thx.default_env(), set_vllm_model_wrapper_context(
                    kv_caches=None, mesh=self.mesh):
                original_lora_metadata = replace_lora_metadata(
                    self.model, lora_metadata, self.vllm_config.lora_config)
                logits = thx.func.functional_call(
                    self.model,
                    torch_view(params_and_buffers),
                    kwargs={
                        "hidden_state": torch_view(hidden_states),
                    },
                    tie_weights=False,
                )
                replace_lora_metadata(self.model, original_lora_metadata,
                                      self.vllm_config.lora_config)
            return jax_view(logits)
        return compute_logits_func
    
    def build_pooler_func(self) -> PoolerFunc:
        def compute_pooler_output(
            hidden_states: jx.Array,
            pooling_metadata: PoolingMetadata,
            seq_lens: np.ndarray,
        ) -> PoolerOutput:
            assert self._pooler is not None, "Model does not support pooling"
            torch_states: th.Tensor = torch_view(hidden_states)
            with thx.default_env():
                torch_states = torch_states.to('cpu', non_blocking=True)
                pooling_metadata.build_pooling_cursor(
                    seq_lens,
                    th.tensor(seq_lens),
                    device=torch_states.device,
                )
                outputs: list[th.Tensor] = self._pooler(
                    torch_states,
                    pooling_metadata,
                )
                return outputs
        return compute_pooler_output

def load_lora_model(model: nn.Module, vllm_config: VllmConfig,
                    device: str) -> nn.Module:
    if not supports_lora(model):
        raise ValueError(
            f"{model.__class__.__name__} does not support LoRA yet.")
    if supports_multimodal(model):
        log.warning("Regarding multimodal models, vLLM currently "
                       "only supports adding LoRA to language model.")
    
    # Add LoRA Manager to the Model Runner
    lora_manager = LRUCacheWorkerLoRAManager(
        vllm_config,
        device,
        model.embedding_modules,
    )
    return lora_manager, lora_manager.create_lora_manager(model)

# The reason why replace the method is that the set_lora and reset_lora need to
# run under torchax env.
def replace_set_lora(model):
    def _tpu_set_lora(
        self,
        index: int,
        lora_a: th.Tensor,
        lora_b: th.Tensor,
    ):
        with thx.default_env():
            self._original_set_lora(index, lora_a, lora_b)
    
    def _tpu_reset_lora(self, index: int):
        with thx.default_env():
            self._original_reset_lora(index)
    
    for _, module in model.named_modules():
        if isinstance(module, BaseLayerWithLoRA):
            module._original_set_lora = module.set_lora
            module._original_reset_lora = module.reset_lora
            module.set_lora = _tpu_set_lora.__get__(module, module.__class__)
            module.reset_lora = _tpu_reset_lora.__get__(
                module, module.__class__)

def test_snake_type_name_no_module_match_scenario():
    """

    Expected: Return the snake_case version of the class name.
    """
    mock_obj = MagicMock()
    mock_obj.__class__.__name__ = "SuperMetric"
    mock_obj.__class__.__module__ = "my_library.metrics"
    # "super_metric" != "metrics", so it returns the snake case name

    Expected: Prefer the module name over auto-generated snake case.
    """
    mock_obj = MagicMock()
    mock_obj.__class__.__name__ = "KoLeoLoss"
    # Logic: snake("KoLeoLoss") -> "ko_leo_loss"
    # Stripped: "koleoloss"

    mock_obj.__class__.__module__ = "custom_lib.losses.koleo_loss"
    # Should prefer the module name over the auto-generated snake case:
    assert snake_type_name(mock_obj) == "koleo_loss"

    """
    mock_obj = MagicMock()
    mock_obj.__class__.__name__ = "SimpleThing"
    mock_obj.__class__.__module__ = "simple_thing"
    # snake("SimpleThing") -> "simple_thing"
    # module -> "simple_thing"
    # They match, returns module (which is identical to snake)
    assert snake_type_name(mock_obj) == "simple_thing"
